Use um *mock.Mock por backend para que as expectativas de legacy e storage sejam verificadas de forma independente.

suggestions.summary: The new 'with dual write (…, mode 3)' playlist subtests read only from unified storage, so they would still pass if the async legacy write never happened.
suggestions.content: The new subtests named "with dual write (file/unified/etcd, mode 3)" configure Mode3 but cannot observe the dual-write behavior they are named after: in mode 3, DualWriterMode3.Get/List read only from unified Storage (dualwriter_mode3.go:63–92), and the legacy write is a fire-and-forget goroutine (dualwriter_mode3.go:50–57) that the test never waits on — doPlaylistTests' assertions are all served from unified storage, so a broken/silent-failure legacy write leaves these subtests green. To actually cover mode 3's dual-write, after doPlaylistTests (or per-operation) wait for the async legacy write and assert the object exists in the legacy store (e.g., query the legacy SQL/file store with require.Eventually); otherwise these subtests are equivalent to the mode-0/mode-2 runs.
suggestions.summaryPt: Os novos subtestes 'with dual write (…, mode 3)' de playlist leem apenas do storage unificado, então ainda passariam se a escrita legacy assíncrona nunca acontecesse.
suggestions.contentPt: Os novos subtestes chamados "with dual write (file/unified/etcd, mode 3)" configuram o Mode3 mas não conseguem observar o comportamento de dual-write que dá nome a eles: no modo 3, DualWriterMode3.Get/List leem apenas do Storage unificado (dualwriter_mode3.go:63–92), e a escrita legacy é uma goroutine fire-and-forget (dualwriter_mode3.go:50–57) que o teste nunca aguarda — todas as asserções de doPlaylistTests são atendidas pelo storage unificado, então uma escrita legacy quebrada/com falha silenciosa deixa esses subtestes verdes. Para realmente cobrir o dual-write do modo 3, após doPlaylistTests (ou por operação) aguarde a escrita legacy assíncrona e verifique que o objeto existe no store legacy (ex.: consulte o store legacy SQL/arquivo com require.Eventually); caso contrário, esses subtestes equivalem às execuções dos modos 0/2.

suggestions.summary: Async legacy writes inherit the request context, which is cancelled as soon as the handler returns, so legacy writes race request teardown and silently fail.
suggestions.content: The legacy-write goroutines in Create (50-57), Delete (108-114), Update (134-141) and DeleteCollection (161-167) do `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)` where `ctx` is the incoming *request* context. In net/http the request context is cancelled when ServeHTTP returns — i.e. right after Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection return to the apiserver handler. The child timeout context is therefore cancelled almost immediately; the legacy write usually fails with `context canceled`, the error is swallowed (only recorded into a metric), and legacy storage silently diverges from unified storage — the exact invariant mode 3 exists to maintain. Legacy-API readers then see stale/missing objects, and there is no retry. The unit tests never catch this because they pass context.Background(), which is never cancelled. Detach from the request's cancellation before applying the timeout (Go >= 1.21 `context.WithoutCancel`), or keep values but drop cancellation, e.g. build the timeout from a detached context.
suggestions.summaryPt: As escritas legacy assíncronas herdam o contexto da requisição, que é cancelado assim que o handler retorna, então as escritas legacy competem com o encerramento da requisição e falham silenciosamente.
suggestions.contentPt: As goroutines de escrita legacy em Create (50-57), Delete (108-114), Update (134-141) e DeleteCollection (161-167) fazem `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)` onde `ctx` é o contexto da *requisição* recebida. No net/http, o contexto da requisição é cancelado quando ServeHTTP retorna — ou seja, logo após Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection retornarem ao handler do apiserver. O contexto filho com timeout é, portanto, cancelado quase imediatamente; a escrita legacy normalmente falha com `context canceled`, o erro é engolido (apenas registrado em uma métrica), e o storage legacy diverge silenciosamente do storage unificado — exatamente o invariante que o modo 3 existe para manter. Leitores da API legacy então veem objetos desatualizados/ausentes, e não há retry. Os testes unitários nunca detectam isso porque passam context.Background(), que nunca é cancelado. Desacople do cancelamento da requisição antes de aplicar o timeout (Go >= 1.21 `context.WithoutCancel`), ou mantenha os valores mas descarte o cancelamento, ex.: construa o timeout a partir de um contexto desacoplado.

suggestions.summary: Fire-and-forget legacy goroutines allow writes to reach legacy storage out of order, leaving it with an older object version than unified storage.
suggestions.content: Because the response is returned (line 116) before the legacy write goroutine (108-114) is guaranteed to have run — and never awaited — a client that sequentially issues Update A, gets its 200, then issues Update A' can have the two legacy goroutines execute in either order. Legacy storage can end with A (older) while unified holds A' (newer). The same hazard exists for a delete followed by a re-create of the same name: the legacy delete may land after the legacy create and remove the new object. Synchronous dual-writes (as in mode 1/2 and the previous implementation) guaranteed legacy was written before the response. Serialize the legacy writes (single worker queue per dual writer or per resource) or keep them synchronous to preserve ordering.
suggestions.summaryPt: Goroutines legacy fire-and-forget permitem que escritas cheguem ao storage legacy fora de ordem, deixando-o com uma versão mais antiga do objeto que o storage unificado.
suggestions.contentPt: Como a resposta é retornada (linha 116) antes de a goroutine de escrita legacy (108-114) ter garantia de execução — e nunca é aguardada — um cliente que emite sequencialmente Update A, recebe seu 200, e depois emite Update A' pode ter as duas goroutines legacy executadas em qualquer ordem. O storage legacy pode terminar com A (mais antigo) enquanto o unificado tem A' (mais novo). O mesmo risco existe para um delete seguido de re-create do mesmo nome: o delete legacy pode chegar depois do create legacy e remover o novo objeto. Dual-writes síncronos (como nos modos 1/2 e na implementação anterior) garantiam que o legacy fosse escrito antes da resposta. Serialize as escritas legacy (fila com um único worker por dual writer ou por recurso) ou mantenha-as síncronas para preservar a ordenação.

suggestions.summary: Multiple metric calls record the wrong storage/backend or the wrong label: storage failures recorded as legacy, a legacy op recorded as storage, and the object name passed as the kind label.
suggestions.content: Four recording calls corrupt the dual-write metrics that operators rely on to decide when it is safe to migrate modes: (a) line 45 — a *storage* Create failure is recorded via recordLegacyDuration(true, ...), inflating legacy error counts; (b) line 129 — same bug for Update's storage failure; (c) line 166 — the *legacy* DeleteCollection is recorded via recordStorageDuration(...), polluting storage duration histograms with legacy timings; (d) line 106 — Delete's success path passes the object `name` as the kind argument while the sibling error path (line 103) passes `options.Kind`; besides being inconsistent for the same metric series, object names are unbounded user-controlled strings, so they land in a Prometheus label and blow up cardinality. Fix each call to use the correct recorder (recordStorageDuration for storage outcomes, recordLegacyDuration for legacy outcomes) and `options.Kind` consistently.
suggestions.summaryPt: Várias chamadas de métrica registram o storage/backend errado ou o label errado: falhas de storage registradas como legacy, uma operação legacy registrada como storage, e o nome do objeto passado como label de kind.
suggestions.contentPt: Quatro chamadas de registro corrompem as métricas de dual-write nas quais os operadores confiam para decidir quando é seguro migrar de modo: (a) linha 45 — uma falha de Create no *storage* é registrada via recordLegacyDuration(true, ...), inflando a contagem de erros de legacy; (b) linha 129 — o mesmo bug para a falha de storage de Update; (c) linha 166 — o DeleteCollection *legacy* é registrado via recordStorageDuration(...), poluindo os histogramas de duração do storage com tempos do legacy; (d) linha 106 — o caminho de sucesso de Delete passa o `name` do objeto como argumento kind enquanto o caminho de erro irmão (linha 103) passa `options.Kind`; além de inconsistente para a mesma série de métrica, nomes de objeto são strings ilimitadas controladas pelo usuário, então acabam em um label do Prometheus e explodem a cardinalidade. Corrija cada chamada para usar o recorder correto (recordStorageDuration para resultados de storage, recordLegacyDuration para resultados de legacy) e `options.Kind` de forma consistente.

suggestions.summary: Update no longer wraps objInfo with updateWrapper, so legacy re-computes the updated object from its own state and can store different content than unified storage committed.
suggestions.content: The previous implementation passed `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}` to Legacy.Update so both stores committed the exact object unified computed. The new goroutine (line 139) passes the raw `objInfo`, so legacy re-invokes `objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` against legacy's own current object. If the two stores are (transiently) diverged — the normal state mode 3 tolerates — a patch-style UpdatedObjectInfo produces a different result for legacy than for unified, making the divergence permanent instead of converging. Also note this runs under the request-cancelled context from the first finding. Restore the updateWrapper (or equivalent) so legacy stores the object unified actually committed.
suggestions.summaryPt: Update não envolve mais o objInfo com updateWrapper, então o legacy recalcula o objeto atualizado a partir do seu próprio estado e pode armazenar conteúdo diferente do que o storage unificado confirmou.
suggestions.contentPt: A implementação anterior passava `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}` para Legacy.Update, de modo que ambos os stores confirmavam exatamente o objeto calculado pelo unificado. A nova goroutine (linha 139) passa o `objInfo` cru, então o legacy reinvoca `objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` contra o seu próprio objeto atual. Se os dois stores estiverem (transitoriamente) divergentes — o estado normal que o modo 3 tolera — um UpdatedObjectInfo estilo patch produz um resultado diferente para o legacy e para o unificado, tornando a divergência permanente em vez de convergir. Note também que isso roda sob o contexto cancelado pela requisição do primeiro achado. Restaure o updateWrapper (ou equivalente) para que o legacy armazene o objeto que o unificado realmente confirmou.

suggestions.summary: Async legacy dual-writes reuse the request context, which is canceled the moment the handler returns, so the background legacy write almost always aborts and mode-3 legacy writes silently never happen.
suggestions.content: The new fire-and-forget legacy writes derive their context from the request-scoped ctx (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) at :51, and the same pattern at :110, :135, :163). The request context is canceled as soon as the REST handler returns and the HTTP response is written, so the background d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection call races against its parent's cancellation and will typically abort with 'context canceled' — the 10s timeout is moot. Before this PR the legacy write ran synchronously with a live context, so callers (legacy SQL-backed Grafana APIs reading the legacy copy) could rely on mode-3 dual writes actually reaching legacy storage; that contract is now silently broken and legacy writes essentially never land in production. Detach from the request lifecycle: build the timeout from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (or context.Background()) before launching each goroutine.
suggestions.summaryPt: As dual-writes legacy assíncronas reutilizam o contexto da requisição, que é cancelado no momento em que o handler retorna, então a escrita legacy em background quase sempre aborta e as escritas legacy do modo 3 silenciosamente nunca acontecem.
suggestions.contentPt: As novas escritas legacy fire-and-forget derivam seu contexto do ctx com escopo de requisição (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) em :51, e o mesmo padrão em :110, :135, :163). O contexto da requisição é cancelado assim que o handler REST retorna e a resposta HTTP é escrita, então a chamada de background d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection compete com o cancelamento do pai e tipicamente abortará com 'context canceled' — o timeout de 10s é irrelevante. Antes deste PR, a escrita legacy rodava de forma síncrona com um contexto vivo, então os chamadores (APIs legacy do Grafana baseadas em SQL que leem a cópia legacy) podiam confiar que as dual-writes do modo 3 realmente chegavam ao storage legacy; esse contrato agora está silenciosamente quebrado e as escritas legacy essencialmente nunca se efetivam em produção. Desacople do ciclo de vida da requisição: construa o timeout a partir de context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (ou context.Background()) antes de iniciar cada goroutine.

suggestions.summary: Update dropped the updateWrapper for the legacy store, so legacy now recomputes the update against its own stale old object and the two stores can persist divergent objects.
suggestions.content: Update no longer passes the storage-computed object to the legacy store. The old implementation computed `updated` once from storage's old object and wrapped it via &updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}, guaranteeing both stores persisted the identical object; mode 2 still does this (dualwriter_mode2.go:298). The new goroutine at :139 calls d.Legacy.Update with the raw objInfo, so legacy re-runs objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, legacyOld) against its own copy — which differs in resourceVersion, timestamps, or content for objects not yet fully mirrored. For patch-style updates the two stores can now persist divergent objects (or legacy fails its RV precondition, or resurrects via forceAllowCreate), losing the 'same object in both stores' guarantee that consumers of the dual-write migration rely on. Restore the updateWrapper for the legacy call (wrapping the object returned by d.Storage.Update at :126).
suggestions.summaryPt: Update removeu o updateWrapper para o store legacy, então o legacy agora recalcula o update contra o seu próprio objeto antigo desatualizado e os dois stores podem persistir objetos divergentes.
suggestions.contentPt: Update não passa mais o objeto calculado pelo storage para o store legacy. A implementação antiga calculava `updated` uma vez a partir do objeto antigo do storage e o envolvia via &updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}, garantindo que ambos os stores persistissem o objeto idêntico; o modo 2 ainda faz isso (dualwriter_mode2.go:298). A nova goroutine em :139 chama d.Legacy.Update com o objInfo cru, então o legacy reexecuta objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, legacyOld) contra sua própria cópia — que difere em resourceVersion, timestamps ou conteúdo para objetos ainda não totalmente espelhados. Para updates estilo patch, os dois stores agora podem persistir objetos divergentes (ou o legacy falha na precondição de RV, ou ressuscita via forceAllowCreate), perdendo a garantia de 'mesmo objeto nos dois stores' da qual dependem os consumidores da migração por dual-write. Restaure o updateWrapper na chamada legacy (envolvendo o objeto retornado por d.Storage.Update em :126).

suggestions.summary: Delete no longer falls through to the legacy store on unified-storage NotFound, leaving pre-migration legacy-only objects permanently uncleaned.
suggestions.content: Delete previously tolerated a NotFound from unified storage (apierrors.IsNotFound) and still proceeded to delete the legacy copy — that path was the only way to clean up objects that exist only in legacy storage (created before mode 3 was enabled for the resource). The new code returns immediately on any storage error at :101-104, before the legacy goroutine at :108 is ever launched, so legacy-only rows become permanently undeletable through the API: the caller gets the same 404 as before but silently loses the legacy-cleanup side effect it used to get. If skipping legacy on storage failure is intentional for non-NotFound errors, at least keep the NotFound case falling through to the legacy delete (or always attempt legacy cleanup, as the old code did).
suggestions.summaryPt: Delete não segue mais para o store legacy em caso de NotFound no storage unificado, deixando objetos pré-migração existentes só no legacy permanentemente sem limpeza.
suggestions.contentPt: Delete anteriormente tolerava um NotFound do storage unificado (apierrors.IsNotFound) e ainda prosseguia para deletar a cópia legacy — esse caminho era a única forma de limpar objetos que existem apenas no storage legacy (criados antes de o modo 3 ser habilitado para o recurso). O novo código retorna imediatamente em qualquer erro de storage em :101-104, antes de a goroutine legacy em :108 ser iniciada, então linhas existentes só no legacy se tornam permanentemente impossíveis de deletar pela API: o chamador recebe o mesmo 404 de antes, mas silenciosamente perde o efeito colateral de limpeza do legacy que antes obtinha. Se pular o legacy em caso de falha de storage é intencional para erros que não sejam NotFound, ao menos mantenha o caso NotFound seguindo para o delete legacy (ou sempre tente a limpeza legacy, como o código antigo fazia).

groups.defect: Metric recorder calls are wrong: the Create and Update storage-error paths call recordLegacyDuration, the DeleteCollection legacy goroutine calls recordStorageDuration, and Delete's success path passes the object name as the kind label.
Update passes the raw objInfo to Legacy.Update instead of an updateWrapper around the storage result, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge from storage.
Delete returns early on a storage NotFound and never deletes the legacy copy, leaving objects that exist only in legacy orphaned.

The fire-and-forget legacy-write goroutines in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection build their timeout context from the request context. That context is canceled when the handler returns, so legacy writes silently abort with context.Canceled. The fix is to detach with context.WithoutCancel.
groups.arbiterReasoning: All four suggestions anchor at dualwriter_mode3.go lines 50-57. Each one names the same defect: the goroutines derive their context from the request context through context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...). Each one lists all four goroutine sites (Create, Delete, Update, DeleteCollection) and gives the same fix, context.WithoutCancel. s_85cdb7f9 also mentions the playlist integration tests and the unit tests that use context.Background(). It does this to explain why the bug isn't caught, not to report a separate defect, so its membership is unaffected. Whether these four belong together is clear. The kind is not. The defect repeats at four places, which looks like systemic_pattern, but every member already covers all four sites and anchors at the same lines. Any single member's comment therefore covers everything, which points to same_location with no unified comment needed. Because the kind is a judgment call, decisive is false.

groups.defect: No mode-3 test checks that the async legacy write happens. The unit tests never assert the legacy mock calls, and the playlist integration subtests only read from unified storage. Removing or breaking the legacy write would leave every test passing.
groups.arbiterReasoning: s_3e0dbc3c and s_952eaebd clearly describe the same defect at the same place: TestMode3_* lines 47-77 never wait for or assert the fire-and-forget legacy write. s_c52e7744 describes the same gap in a different file, the new mode-3 playlist integration subtests. s_952eaebd links the two because it reports the integration gap as part of its own problem, not just as background: its summary says removing the goroutine 'would still pass every unit and integration test', and its explanation names integration tests that read only from unified storage. Chaining through s_952eaebd puts all three in one group. The group is cross_location, not systemic_pattern: this is one test gap seen from the unit-test file and the integration-test file, not a copy-pasted mistake. Those two places need separate edits (mock call assertions vs. querying the legacy store), so the merged comment must keep both, and needsUnifiedComment is true. This is not decisive because s_c52e7744 could also be read as a separate integration-test gap with a different fix.

secondCheck.reasonPt: A s_48464c58 também aponta que as goroutines podem aplicar atualizações concorrentes fora de ordem e causar divergência permanente. Há possível sobreposição com o defeito de ordenação, embora essa observação apareça como agravante da ausência de updateWrapper, que é seu foco principal.

groups.defect: Metric recorder calls are wrong: the Create and Update storage-error paths call recordLegacyDuration, the DeleteCollection legacy goroutine calls recordStorageDuration, and Delete's success path passes the object name as the kind label.
groups.rationale: s_1f0c2877 and s_f5076626 each report all four metric mis-recordings. The other suggestions each report one of them, so the overlap links them all into one group.

groups.defect: The async legacy-write goroutines derive their context from the request context, which is canceled when the handler returns, so legacy writes silently abort.
groups.rationale: All four report the same request-context cancellation problem across the four goroutines and propose the same fix, context.WithoutCancel.

groups.defect: No mode-3 test, unit or integration, checks that the async legacy write actually happens, so removing it would leave every test green.
groups.rationale: All three report the same test gap, the unasserted legacy write. s_952eaebd explicitly covers both the unit and the integration tests, and s_c52e7744 points at the integration subtests.

groups.defect: Update passes the raw objInfo to Legacy.Update instead of an updateWrapper around the storage result, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge from storage.
groups.rationale: All three report the dropped updateWrapper in the Update goroutine and propose restoring it.

groups.defect: Delete returns early on a storage NotFound and never deletes the legacy copy, leaving objects that exist only in legacy orphaned.
groups.rationale: Both report the same lost NotFound fall-through in Delete and propose the same fix.

groups.defect: Mode-3 unit and playlist integration tests never wait for and assert the legacy writes, allowing missing legacy writes to go undetected.
groups.rationale: All report missing verification of the legacy half of dual writes. The unit and integration tests require separate edits, so the merged comment must preserve both locations.

groups.defect: Legacy Update receives raw objInfo instead of the unified store's committed object through updateWrapper, allowing recomputation to diverge or fail.
groups.rationale: All identify the removed wrapper at the same Legacy.Update call. References to request cancellation and asynchronous ordering describe compounding conditions rather than separate findings within these comments.

groups.defect: Create and Update storage failures use the legacy recorder, legacy DeleteCollection uses the storage recorder, and successful Delete uses the object name as the kind label.
groups.rationale: The two comprehensive suggestions explicitly cover all four faulty metric calls, linking the narrower suggestions. Each affected call requires correction.

groups.defect: Delete returns on unified-storage NotFound before attempting legacy cleanup, leaving legacy-only objects undeleted.
groups.rationale: Both report the same removed NotFound exception in Delete's early-return branch.

groups.defect: All four asynchronous legacy write paths inherit request cancellation, allowing handler completion to abort the background writes.
groups.rationale: Each identifies the same request-context lifetime mistake repeated across Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection. The test references explain why cancellation is missed; they do not independently report the missing legacy assertions covered by the test group.

suggestions.summary: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() now returns null, violating the documented GroupModel SPI contract that the count is never null.
suggestions.content: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the underlying model was concurrently deleted (modelSupplier.get() == null), violating the GroupModel SPI contract which explicitly documents "Never returns {@code null}" (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/GroupModel.java:293-300). Any caller that unboxes the result or relies on the documented invariant (including third-party SPI consumers) will throw an NPE at the call site, and it is inconsistent with this class's own handling of a missing delegate (isUpdated()/getDelegateForUpdate() throw IllegalStateException("Not found in database")). Returning 0L would keep the never-null contract while still avoiding the original NPE; alternatively throw IllegalStateException to match the class convention.
suggestions.summaryPt: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() agora retorna null, violando o contrato documentado da SPI GroupModel de que a contagem nunca é null.
suggestions.contentPt: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() agora retorna null quando o modelo subjacente foi excluído concorrentemente (modelSupplier.get() == null), violando o contrato da SPI GroupModel, que documenta explicitamente "Never returns {@code null}" (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/GroupModel.java:293-300). Qualquer chamador que faça unboxing do resultado ou dependa do invariante documentado (incluindo consumidores terceiros da SPI) lançará um NPE no ponto da chamada, e isso é inconsistente com o tratamento da própria classe para um delegate ausente (isUpdated()/getDelegateForUpdate() lançam IllegalStateException("Not found in database")). Retornar 0L manteria o contrato de nunca ser null e ainda evitaria o NPE original; alternativamente, lance IllegalStateException para seguir a convenção da classe.

suggestions.summary: The new concurrency test never joins its reader thread, so the empty-exceptions assertion can pass before the final in-flight read records its failure (and before any read has happened at all).
suggestions.content: The reader thread is never joined: after deletedAll.set(true) (line 155) the main thread immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty (line 157), but the reader thread may still be inside the final groups(...) HTTP call — an exception from that call is added to caughtExceptions AFTER the assertion has already passed, so the test reports success despite the exact concurrent-access failure it was written to catch for issue #40368. Additionally, there is no rendezvous guaranteeing the reader ran at all: a delayed thread scheduling can observe deletedAll==true on the first loop check and execute zero reads, making the test trivially green. Keep a reference to the Thread, call thread.join() after deletedAll.set(true), and (optionally) count iterations and assert at least one read occurred before asserting caughtExceptions is empty.
suggestions.summaryPt: O novo teste de concorrência nunca faz join na thread leitora, então a asserção de exceções vazias pode passar antes que a última leitura em andamento registre sua falha (e até antes de qualquer leitura ter ocorrido).
suggestions.contentPt: A thread leitora nunca recebe join: após deletedAll.set(true) (linha 155), a thread principal imediatamente assere que caughtExceptions está vazio (linha 157), mas a thread leitora ainda pode estar dentro da última chamada HTTP groups(...) — uma exceção dessa chamada é adicionada a caughtExceptions DEPOIS que a asserção já passou, então o teste reporta sucesso apesar da exata falha de acesso concorrente que foi escrito para capturar na issue #40368. Além disso, não há nenhum rendezvous garantindo que a leitora tenha rodado: um atraso no agendamento da thread pode fazer com que ela observe deletedAll==true na primeira verificação do loop e execute zero leituras, deixando o teste trivialmente verde. Mantenha uma referência à Thread, chame thread.join() após deletedAll.set(true) e (opcionalmente) conte as iterações e assegure que ao menos uma leitura ocorreu antes de assegurar que caughtExceptions está vazio.

suggestions.summary: The test concurrently uses one shared RESTEasy RealmResource client proxy from two threads, which is not a documented thread-safe usage and can make the new test flaky.
suggestions.content: The test drives the single shared RealmResource RESTEasy client proxy (managedRealm.admin() returns one cached instance, ManagedRealm.java:39-41) concurrently from two threads — the raw reader thread (line 143) and the main deletion loop (line 153). RESTEasy documentation does not guarantee client proxies / the underlying connection engine are thread-safe (it depends on the connection manager configuration), so concurrent use can produce client-side exceptions that are recorded into caughtExceptions, making the test flaky or masking the server-side signal it intends to measure. Prefer creating a separate Keycloak admin client instance for the reader thread, or verify the shared client's engine is configured for concurrent use.
suggestions.summaryPt: O teste usa concorrentemente um único proxy de cliente RESTEasy RealmResource compartilhado em duas threads, o que não é um uso documentado como thread-safe e pode tornar o novo teste flaky.
suggestions.contentPt: O teste usa o único proxy de cliente RESTEasy RealmResource compartilhado (managedRealm.admin() retorna uma instância em cache, ManagedRealm.java:39-41) concorrentemente em duas threads — a thread leitora bruta (linha 143) e o loop de exclusão principal (linha 153). A documentação do RESTEasy não garante que os proxies de cliente / o connection engine subjacente sejam thread-safe (depende da configuração do connection manager), então o uso concorrente pode produzir exceções no lado do cliente que são registradas em caughtExceptions, tornando o teste flaky ou mascarando o sinal do lado do servidor que ele pretende medir. Prefira criar uma instância separada de cliente admin do Keycloak para a thread leitora, ou verifique se o engine do cliente compartilhado está configurado para uso concorrente.

suggestions.summary: The reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can run before the thread's final in-flight read finishes, letting exceptions be recorded after the check and the test pass while the very bug it hunts occurred.
suggestions.content: The reader thread is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` at line 157. `deletedAll.set(true)` only stops the loop between iterations, so the thread can still be mid-flight in one last `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` call when the assertion runs — an exception thrown by that final read is appended to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion already read the list, so the test can pass even though the failure it is designed to detect just occurred (and can also fail intermittently). Keep the Thread reference and call `thread.join()` (with a timeout) after `deletedAll.set(true)` and before asserting.
suggestions.summaryPt: A thread leitora nunca recebe join, então a asserção pode rodar antes de a última leitura em andamento da thread terminar, permitindo que exceções sejam registradas após a verificação e o teste passe mesmo com o bug que ele procura tendo ocorrido.
suggestions.contentPt: A thread leitora nunca recebe join antes de `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` na linha 157. `deletedAll.set(true)` apenas interrompe o loop entre iterações, então a thread ainda pode estar no meio de uma última chamada `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` quando a asserção roda — uma exceção lançada por essa última leitura é adicionada a `caughtExceptions` depois que a asserção já leu a lista, então o teste pode passar mesmo que a falha que ele foi projetado para detectar tenha acabado de ocorrer (e também pode falhar de forma intermitente). Mantenha a referência da Thread e chame `thread.join()` (com timeout) após `deletedAll.set(true)` e antes de assertar.

suggestions.summary: If any group removal throws, deletedAll is never set and the non-daemon reader thread spins in its unbounded loop forever, hanging the test JVM instead of failing.
suggestions.content: The reader thread's only exit condition is `deletedAll` (line 140), but the flag is set at line 155 in straight-line code after the deletion `forEach` (lines 152-154). If any `remove()` throws — which is exactly the failure mode this test is designed to provoke — the exception propagates out of the test method, `deletedAll.set(true)` never executes, and the non-daemon reader thread spins in its unbounded loop issuing requests forever, hanging the test JVM instead of failing fast. Set the flag in a `finally` block (or bound the loop with a max iteration count / timeout) so the thread always terminates.
suggestions.summaryPt: Se qualquer remoção de grupo lançar exceção, deletedAll nunca é definido e a thread leitora não-daemon fica girando em seu loop ilimitado para sempre, travando a JVM do teste em vez de falhar.
suggestions.contentPt: A única condição de saída da thread leitora é `deletedAll` (linha 140), mas a flag é definida na linha 155 em código linear após o `forEach` de exclusão (linhas 152-154). Se qualquer `remove()` lançar exceção — que é exatamente o modo de falha que este teste foi projetado para provocar — a exceção se propaga para fora do método de teste, `deletedAll.set(true)` nunca é executado, e a thread leitora não-daemon fica girando em seu loop ilimitado emitindo requisições para sempre, travando a JVM do teste em vez de falhar rapidamente. Defina a flag em um bloco `finally` (ou limite o loop com um número máximo de iterações / timeout) para que a thread sempre termine.

suggestions.content: The reader thread is never joined, and the assertion races with it: `deletedAll.set(true)` (line 155) followed immediately by `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` (line 157) can evaluate the list before the reader thread records the exception from its final in-flight `groups(...)` call (a read that started while the flag was still false). The test can therefore pass despite an observed failure — a false pass for precisely the concurrent read/delete regression it was written to guard. The thread also continues running past the assertion and can leak into subsequent test teardown. Fix: hold a reference to the Thread (e.g., `Thread reader = new Thread(...)`), call `deletedAll.set(true)`, then `reader.join(10_000)` before asserting, so every read that overlapped the deletion window is counted. Optionally also track the number of reads performed before `deletedAll` was set and assert it is > 0, so a run where the reader thread was scheduled late cannot trivially pass without measuring anything.
suggestions.contentPt: A thread leitora nunca recebe join, e a asserção compete com ela (race): `deletedAll.set(true)` (linha 155) seguido imediatamente por `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` (linha 157) pode avaliar a lista antes que a thread leitora registre a exceção de sua última chamada `groups(...)` em andamento (uma leitura que começou enquanto a flag ainda era false). O teste pode, portanto, passar apesar de uma falha observada — um falso positivo exatamente para a regressão de leitura/exclusão concorrente que ele foi escrito para proteger. A thread também continua rodando após a asserção e pode vazar para o teardown de testes subsequentes. Correção: mantenha uma referência à Thread (por exemplo, `Thread reader = new Thread(...)`), chame `deletedAll.set(true)` e então `reader.join(10_000)` antes de assertar, de modo que toda leitura que se sobrepôs à janela de exclusão seja contabilizada. Opcionalmente, também registre o número de leituras realizadas antes de `deletedAll` ser definido e assegure que seja > 0, para que uma execução em que a thread leitora foi agendada tarde não possa passar trivialmente sem medir nada.

suggestions.summary: The reader thread is never joined, so the final in-flight read can throw the exact bug being tested after the assertion has already passed.
suggestions.content: The reader thread is never joined and there is no barrier between starting it and the deletion loop, so the assertion at line 157 can execute before the work it is about has finished. The reader's last iteration is allowed to still be inside its HTTP call when deletedAll is set: if that call throws the very exception this test exists to detect (e.g. an NPE from the unfixed getSubGroupsCount path), it is appended to caughtExceptions after assertThat has already evaluated, and the test passes. Fix by keeping a reference to the thread and calling join() (with a timeout) after deletedAll.set(true) and before the assertion, so every recorded exception is visible to the assertion; also make the thread a daemon and interrupt/join it in all cases so it cannot linger into subsequent tests.
suggestions.summaryPt: A thread leitora nunca recebe join, então a última leitura em andamento pode lançar o exato bug testado depois que a asserção já passou.
suggestions.contentPt: A thread leitora nunca recebe join e não há barreira entre iniciá-la e o loop de exclusão, então a asserção na linha 157 pode executar antes de o trabalho ao qual ela se refere ter terminado. A última iteração da leitora pode ainda estar dentro de sua chamada HTTP quando deletedAll é definido: se essa chamada lançar a própria exceção que este teste existe para detectar (por exemplo, um NPE do caminho getSubGroupsCount sem a correção), ela é adicionada a caughtExceptions depois que assertThat já avaliou, e o teste passa. Corrija mantendo uma referência à thread e chamando join() (com timeout) após deletedAll.set(true) e antes da asserção, para que toda exceção registrada seja visível para a asserção; além disso, torne a thread daemon e faça interrupt/join dela em todos os casos para que não persista em testes subsequentes.

suggestions.summary: The test can pass with zero reads overlapping the deletions because the reader is not gated to start before deletion and no check verifies any read occurred.
suggestions.content: Nothing guarantees a single read iteration overlaps the deletion phase: the reader loop's first check of deletedAll (line 140) can happen after the main thread already finished all deletions (slow thread start, loaded CI runner), in which case the loop body never executes, caughtExceptions is trivially empty, and the test passes without ever exercising the concurrent read-while-deleting window it is named for. Add a start barrier (e.g. CountDownLatch awaited after Thread.start() before the deletion loop) and record an iteration counter, asserting at the end that at least one read actually occurred during the deletion phase — otherwise the empty-exceptions assertion is vacuous.
suggestions.summaryPt: O teste pode passar com zero leituras sobrepostas às exclusões porque a leitora não é condicionada a iniciar antes da exclusão e nenhuma verificação confirma que alguma leitura ocorreu.
suggestions.contentPt: Nada garante que uma única iteração de leitura se sobreponha à fase de exclusão: a primeira verificação de deletedAll no loop da leitora (linha 140) pode acontecer depois que a thread principal já terminou todas as exclusões (início lento da thread, runner de CI carregado), caso em que o corpo do loop nunca executa, caughtExceptions fica trivialmente vazio, e o teste passa sem nunca exercitar a janela de leitura concorrente durante a exclusão para a qual ele foi nomeado. Adicione uma start barrier (por exemplo, um CountDownLatch aguardado após Thread.start() antes do loop de exclusão) e registre um contador de iterações, assegurando ao final que ao menos uma leitura realmente ocorreu durante a fase de exclusão — caso contrário, a asserção de exceções vazias é vazia de significado.

groups.defect: The reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can run before an exception from its final in-flight read is recorded (false pass). Also, nothing guarantees the reader ran even once during the deletions, so the test can pass without testing anything.

The reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can run before an exception from its final in-flight read is recorded (false pass). Also, nothing guarantees the reader ran even once during the deletions, so the test can pass without testing anything.
groups.rationale: Four suggestions report the missing join and assertion race. s_4875e870 also reports the zero-reads problem as a defect, which links it to s_609a1176, so all five go in one group through that chain.

groups.defect: The test does not wait for the reader to finish before asserting, allowing late exceptions and reader activity during teardown, and does not ensure any read occurs during deletion, allowing a vacuous pass.
groups.rationale: The first four suggestions share the missing-join assertion race. s_4875e870 also explicitly reports the zero-read execution defect described by s_609a1176, connecting both defects into one overlapping group.

suggestions.summary: Client deletion fails with UnsupportedOperationException when both FGAP V1 and V2 features are enabled
suggestions.content: WHAT: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195) throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener (AdminPermissions.java:77-91, modified in this PR) calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent, guarded only by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag, while AdminPermissions.management() (AdminPermissions.java:66-71) selects MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. WHY: with both features enabled at once (a valid combination — Profile.java:58 declares ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 as a separate experimental feature depending only on Feature.AUTHORIZATION), every client removal publishes the event (JpaRealmProvider.java:1006) and DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.publish (DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.java:86-90) iterates listeners without any try/catch, so the UnsupportedOperationException propagates and aborts the DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} transaction — client deletion becomes impossible. Secondary: in V2-only mode the guard silently skips cleanup, leaving orphaned per-client resources/permissions for deleted clients. HOW: also skip the listener when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled (or make ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) a no-op/delete-the-resource implementation instead of throwing).
suggestions.summaryPt: A exclusão de client falha com UnsupportedOperationException quando as features FGAP V1 e V2 estão ambas habilitadas
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195) lança UnsupportedOperationException, mas AdminPermissions.registerListener (AdminPermissions.java:77-91, modificado neste PR) chama management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) a cada ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent, protegido apenas pela feature flag ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), enquanto AdminPermissions.management() (AdminPermissions.java:66-71) seleciona MgmtPermissionsV2 sempre que ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 está habilitada. POR QUÊ: com ambas as features habilitadas ao mesmo tempo (uma combinação válida — Profile.java:58 declara ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 como uma feature experimental separada que depende apenas de Feature.AUTHORIZATION), toda remoção de client publica o evento (JpaRealmProvider.java:1006) e DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.publish (DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.java:86-90) itera os listeners sem nenhum try/catch, então a UnsupportedOperationException se propaga e aborta a transação de DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} — a exclusão de client se torna impossível. Secundário: no modo somente V2, a guarda ignora silenciosamente a limpeza, deixando resources/permissions por client órfãos para clients excluídos. COMO: também ignorar o listener quando ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 estiver habilitada (ou fazer ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) ser um no-op/uma implementação que exclui o resource, em vez de lançar exceção).

suggestions.summary: getClientsWithPermission can return the non-client-ID string "Clients" (and misses per-client resources), causing an NPE in its only caller
suggestions.content: WHAT: getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:138-144) enumerates resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and adds resource.getName() to the returned set, but per-client resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:103-111) never have a `type` attribute set (only create(server, name, owner) + updateScopes), so per-client grants are not matched by the type query; meanwhile the schema-level "Clients" type resource does match the query, so when an all-clients scope permission grants the requested scope the literal string "Clients" — not a client UUID — is added to the result. WHY: the only production caller, AvailableRoleMappingResource.getRoleIdsWithPermissions (rest/admin-ui-ext/.../AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229-230), dereferences every entry via realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream(), so the bogus "Clients" entry (or entries for deleted clients, since the V2 listener no longer cleans up resources on client removal) causes a NullPointerException/500 on the admin console available-role-mapping endpoints; and for admins holding only per-client map-roles permissions the returned set is silently empty, so available client roles are never listed. This breaks the V1 contract (ClientPermissions.java:667-687) where the method returns real client IDs (type "Client" + "client.resource." prefix stripping). HOW: skip the type resource in the findByType consumer (exclude the resource whose name equals CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and ensure per-client resources are created with type=CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE (e.g. resource.setType(...) in getOrCreateResource) so the enumeration only yields valid client IDs.
suggestions.summaryPt: getClientsWithPermission pode retornar a string "Clients" (que não é um client ID) e não encontra resources por client, causando um NPE no seu único chamador
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:138-144) enumera resources com resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) e adiciona resource.getName() ao set retornado, mas os resources por client criados por AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:103-111) nunca têm o atributo `type` definido (apenas create(server, name, owner) + updateScopes), então as permissões por client não são encontradas pela consulta por type; enquanto isso, o resource de type "Clients" no nível do schema corresponde à consulta, então quando uma scope permission de todos os clients concede o scope solicitado, a string literal "Clients" — e não um UUID de client — é adicionada ao resultado. POR QUÊ: o único chamador em produção, AvailableRoleMappingResource.getRoleIdsWithPermissions (rest/admin-ui-ext/.../AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229-230), desreferencia cada entrada via realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream(), então a entrada falsa "Clients" (ou entradas de clients excluídos, já que o listener V2 não limpa mais os resources na remoção do client) causa uma NullPointerException/500 nos endpoints de available-role-mapping do console admin; e para admins que têm apenas permissões map-roles por client, o set retornado fica silenciosamente vazio, então os client roles disponíveis nunca são listados. Isso quebra o contrato da V1 (ClientPermissions.java:667-687), em que o método retorna client IDs reais (type "Client" + remoção do prefixo "client.resource."). COMO: ignorar o resource de type no consumer de findByType (excluir o resource cujo nome é igual a CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) e garantir que os resources por client sejam criados com type=CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE (por exemplo, resource.setType(...) em getOrCreateResource), para que a enumeração produza apenas client IDs válidos.

suggestions.summary: Realm-wide canView() ignores all-clients manage permission, causing 403s for manage-all admins
suggestions.content: WHAT: the realm-wide canView() override (ClientPermissionsV2.java:86-88) accepts only the all-clients `view` scope, so a fine-grained admin granted only all-clients `manage` fails every realm-wide view check. WHY: requireList()/requireListClientScopes()/requireViewClientScopes() funnel through canView() — e.g. GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients throws 403 at ClientsResource.java:120 (auth.clients().requireList()), and client-scope listing throws 403 via canViewClientScopes() → canView() — even though the same admin can create, update and delete every client because canManage() (line 73) and canManageClientScopes() (line 109) do honor the manage scope. PermissionClientTest.testManageAllClients only passes because myadmin additionally holds the QUERY_USERS role (RealmAdminPermissionsConfig.java:34). This is inconsistent with the sibling UserPermissionsV2.canView (UserPermissionsV2.java:52) which treats manage as implying view by passing both VIEW and MANAGE scopes, and with this class's own canView(ClientScopeModel) (line 121) which checks VIEW || MANAGE. HOW: include the manage scope, e.g. `return canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW) || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` (or delegate to canManageClientScopes()).
suggestions.summaryPt: O canView() no nível do realm ignora a permissão manage de todos os clients, causando 403 para admins com manage-all
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: o override de canView() no nível do realm (ClientPermissionsV2.java:86-88) aceita apenas o scope `view` de todos os clients, então um admin fine-grained com apenas `manage` de todos os clients falha em toda verificação de view no nível do realm. POR QUÊ: requireList()/requireListClientScopes()/requireViewClientScopes() passam por canView() — por exemplo, GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients lança 403 em ClientsResource.java:120 (auth.clients().requireList()), e a listagem de client scopes lança 403 via canViewClientScopes() → canView() — mesmo que o mesmo admin consiga criar, atualizar e excluir todos os clients, porque canManage() (linha 73) e canManageClientScopes() (linha 109) respeitam o scope manage. PermissionClientTest.testManageAllClients só passa porque myadmin também possui o role QUERY_USERS (RealmAdminPermissionsConfig.java:34). Isso é inconsistente com o UserPermissionsV2.canView irmão (UserPermissionsV2.java:52), que trata manage como implicando view ao passar os scopes VIEW e MANAGE, e com o próprio canView(ClientScopeModel) desta classe (linha 121), que verifica VIEW || MANAGE. COMO: incluir o scope manage, por exemplo `return canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW) || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` (ou delegar para canManageClientScopes()).

suggestions.summary: Possible null resource passed to findByResource when the "Clients" type resource does not exist
suggestions.content: WHAT: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) (ClientPermissionsV2.java:215-221) assigns the result of AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and passes it unchecked into policyStore.findByResource(server, resource), but getResourceTypeResource only performs findByName and returns null when the "Clients" type resource does not exist (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:116-134 — it never creates). WHY: any realm whose admin-permissions resource server was initialized before this PR added the Clients type is missing that resource — SCHEMA.init only runs at realm creation (RealmManager.java:572), and the adminPermissionsClient import path (RealmManager.java:567-570) creates the resource server while skipping SCHEMA.init entirely — so every per-client check (canManage/canView/canConfigure/canMapRoles on a client that has no per-client resource) dereferences the null resource inside findByResource and throws, turning admin client operations into 500s. The sibling hasPermission(String) overload in the same file (ClientPermissionsV2.java:244-247) does null-check, so the asymmetry looks unintended. HOW: after line 217 add `if (resource == null) return false;` mirroring lines 245-247.
suggestions.summaryPt: Possível resource null passado para findByResource quando o resource de type "Clients" não existe
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) (ClientPermissionsV2.java:215-221) atribui o resultado de AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) e o passa sem verificação para policyStore.findByResource(server, resource), mas getResourceTypeResource apenas executa findByName e retorna null quando o resource de type "Clients" não existe (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:116-134 — nunca o cria). POR QUÊ: qualquer realm cujo resource server de admin-permissions foi inicializado antes de este PR adicionar o type Clients não possui esse resource — SCHEMA.init só roda na criação do realm (RealmManager.java:572), e o caminho de importação do adminPermissionsClient (RealmManager.java:567-570) cria o resource server ignorando SCHEMA.init por completo — então toda verificação por client (canManage/canView/canConfigure/canMapRoles em um client que não tem resource por client) desreferencia o resource null dentro de findByResource e lança exceção, transformando operações admin de client em 500. A sobrecarga irmã hasPermission(String) no mesmo arquivo (ClientPermissionsV2.java:244-247) faz null check, então a assimetria parece não intencional. COMO: após a linha 217, adicionar `if (resource == null) return false;`, espelhando as linhas 245-247.

suggestions.summary: Javadoc for the void method requireView() claims it returns a boolean instead of documenting that it throws ForbiddenException on denial.
suggestions.content: The javadoc added for `void requireView()` reads "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.", but the method is void and its actual contract is to throw ForbiddenException when canView() returns false — exactly as documented for every other require* method in this same PR (requireManage(), requireList(), requireConfigure(ClientModel), requireView(ClientModel), etc.). The doc block describes a return shape the method cannot produce, so a caller reading the interface would mistake it for a boolean predicate. It should read: "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}."
suggestions.summaryPt: O Javadoc do método void requireView() afirma que ele retorna um boolean, em vez de documentar que lança ForbiddenException em caso de negação.
suggestions.contentPt: O Javadoc adicionado para `void requireView()` diz "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.", mas o método é void e seu contrato real é lançar ForbiddenException quando canView() retorna false — exatamente como documentado para todos os outros métodos require* neste mesmo PR (requireManage(), requireList(), requireConfigure(ClientModel), requireView(ClientModel), etc.). O bloco de documentação descreve um retorno que o método não pode produzir, então um chamador que leia a interface pode confundi-lo com um predicado boolean. Deveria dizer: "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}."
