suggestions.content: WHAT: `execute(...)[0]['id']` (and the same for `uncategorized_category_id` at line 15) assumes the query returns a row. If `embed_category` was never set, or its value doesn't match a category name, the result is empty. WHY: indexing an empty PG::Result raises (IndexError, or nil['id'] NoMethodError), so the migration aborts and the deploy fails on every site that never configured embed_category. The `category_id == 0` fallback is never reached. HOW: check `result.ntuples > 0` (or use `select_value`) and fall back to uncategorized when there is no row.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: `execute(...)[0]['id']` (e o mesmo para `uncategorized_category_id` na linha 15) assume que a query retorna uma linha. Se `embed_category` nunca foi definido, ou se seu valor não corresponde a um nome de categoria, o resultado é vazio. POR QUÊ: acessar o índice de um PG::Result vazio lança erro (IndexError, ou NoMethodError em nil['id']), então a migration aborta e o deploy falha em todo site que nunca configurou embed_category. O fallback `category_id == 0` nunca é alcançado. CORREÇÃO: verifique `result.ntuples > 0` (ou use `select_value`) e use uncategorized como fallback quando não houver linha.

suggestions.content: WHAT: hosts from the old setting are split on "\n" and inserted as-is through string interpolation. They skip the model's normalization (stripping http(s):// and paths), keep trailing \r and whitespace, and are not quoted. WHY: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` matches `lower(host)` against `URI#host`, so a migrated value like `http://example.com` or `example.com\r` never matches and embedding silently breaks after upgrade. A value containing a quote breaks the INSERT and aborts the migration. HOW: strip and normalize each value (`h.strip.sub(%r{^https?://}, '').sub(%r{/.*$}, '')`), skip blanks, and escape it with `quote(h)`.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: os hosts da configuração antiga são separados por "\n" e inseridos como estão via interpolação de string. Eles pulam a normalização do model (remoção de http(s):// e paths), mantêm `\r` e espaços em branco no final, e não são escapados com aspas. POR QUÊ: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compara `lower(host)` com `URI#host`, então um valor migrado como `http://example.com` ou `example.com\r` nunca corresponde e o embedding quebra silenciosamente após o upgrade. Um valor contendo aspas quebra o INSERT e aborta a migration. CORREÇÃO: aplique strip e normalize cada valor (`h.strip.sub(%r{^https?://}, '').sub(%r{/.*$}, '')`), ignore valores em branco e escape com `quote(h)`.

suggestions.content: WHAT: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the column, not `uri.host`. It also compares the bare host, while the validator allows stored hosts with a `:port` suffix. WHY: a referer or embed URL with uppercase letters, or any host saved with a port (e.g. `localhost.dev:3000`), never matches, so `host_allowed?` returns false and embedding/TopicRetriever are rejected. HOW: use `host.downcase`, and compare against `uri.host` plus `"#{uri.host}:#{uri.port}"` (or store the port separately).
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` converte para minúsculas apenas a coluna, não `uri.host`. Também compara apenas o host puro, enquanto o validator permite hosts armazenados com sufixo `:port`. POR QUÊ: um referer ou URL de embed com letras maiúsculas, ou qualquer host salvo com porta (ex.: `localhost.dev:3000`), nunca corresponde, então `host_allowed?` retorna false e embedding/TopicRetriever são rejeitados. CORREÇÃO: use `host.downcase` e compare com `uri.host` mais `"#{uri.host}:#{uri.port}"` (ou armazene a porta separadamente).

suggestions.content: WHAT: the `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!` with no nil guard. `save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, which can be nil. WHY: a create/update request without a host raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. HOW: `return if host.blank?`, or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: o callback `before_validation` chama `self.host.sub!` sem nil guard. `save_host` atribui `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` diretamente, que pode ser nil. POR QUÊ: uma requisição de create/update sem host lança NoMethodError, gerando um 500 em vez de um erro de validação. CORREÇÃO: `return if host.blank?`, ou use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

suggestions.content: WHAT: `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and dereference the result immediately. WHY: an unknown or already-deleted id (e.g. double-delete from two admin tabs) raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of a 404. HOW: use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])`, or raise `Discourse::NotFound` when nil.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: `update` e `destroy` usam `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` e acessam o resultado imediatamente. POR QUÊ: um id desconhecido ou já excluído (ex.: exclusão dupla a partir de duas abas de admin) lança NoMethodError em nil e retorna 500 em vez de 404. CORREÇÃO: use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])`, ou lance `Discourse::NotFound` quando for nil.

suggestions.content: WHAT: every key matching `*_ids` is now mapped through `_lookupSubType` and the original key is always deleted. Ids that can't be resolved become `undefined` entries, and a null `*_ids` value throws on `.map`. WHY: existing REST models with `*_ids` fields lose that data (replaced by arrays of undefined) or crash during hydration when no matching sideloaded collection exists. `hydrated || []` is dead code because `map` always returns an array. HOW: guard with `Array.isArray(obj[k])`, only replace/delete when the sideloaded collection exists, and filter out unresolved ids.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: toda chave que corresponde a `*_ids` agora é mapeada via `_lookupSubType` e a chave original é sempre removida. Ids que não podem ser resolvidos viram entradas `undefined`, e um valor `*_ids` nulo lança erro em `.map`. POR QUÊ: models REST existentes com campos `*_ids` perdem esses dados (substituídos por arrays de undefined) ou quebram durante a hidratação quando não existe coleção sideloaded correspondente. `hydrated || []` é código morto porque `map` sempre retorna um array. CORREÇÃO: proteja com `Array.isArray(obj[k])`, só substitua/remova quando a coleção sideloaded existir, e filtre os ids não resolvidos.

suggestions.content: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the INNER JOIN returns a row. When no `embed_category` setting is stored (the default case), or its value doesn't match a category name, the result is empty. Indexing an empty PG::Result at 0 raises an error, so the migration crashes before reaching the `category_id == 0` fallback. The `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15 has the same problem. Check `ntuples`/`cmd_tuples` before indexing, as the code already does for the `embeddable_hosts` query.
suggestions.contentPt: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assume que o INNER JOIN retorna uma linha. Quando nenhuma configuração `embed_category` está armazenada (o caso padrão), ou seu valor não corresponde a um nome de categoria, o resultado é vazio. Acessar o índice 0 de um PG::Result vazio lança erro, então a migration quebra antes de alcançar o fallback `category_id == 0`. A busca de `uncategorized_category_id` na linha 15 tem o mesmo problema. Verifique `ntuples`/`cmd_tuples` antes de acessar o índice, como o código já faz para a query de `embeddable_hosts`.

suggestions.content: The new `_ids` branch calls `obj[k].map(...)` without checking that the value is an array. A payload with `something_ids: null` throws a TypeError and breaks hydration of the whole response. The `|| []` guard is applied to the result of `map`, which is always an array, so it never takes effect. Guard the input instead (`(obj[k] || []).map(...)`), and consider dropping ids that `_lookupSubType` can't resolve so they don't stay in the array as `undefined`.
suggestions.contentPt: O novo branch de `_ids` chama `obj[k].map(...)` sem verificar se o valor é um array. Um payload com `something_ids: null` lança TypeError e quebra a hidratação da resposta inteira. O guard `|| []` é aplicado ao resultado de `map`, que sempre é um array, então nunca tem efeito. Proteja a entrada (`(obj[k] || []).map(...)`) e considere descartar ids que `_lookupSubType` não consegue resolver, para que não permaneçam no array como `undefined`.

suggestions.summary: The query lowercases the stored host but not the incoming URI host, so referers with mixed-case hostnames are rejected.
suggestions.content: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the stored column. The incoming `uri.host` keeps whatever case it arrived with, because Ruby's URI does not downcase hosts. A referer or embed_url like `http://EvilTrout.com/page` therefore fails host_allowed?, which blocks embedding and topic retrieval, and TopicEmbed.import falls back to no category. Lowercase both sides of the comparison.
suggestions.summaryPt: A query converte para minúsculas o host armazenado, mas não o host da URI recebida, então referers com hostnames em caixa mista são rejeitados.
suggestions.contentPt: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` converte para minúsculas apenas a coluna armazenada. O `uri.host` recebido mantém a caixa com que chegou, porque o URI do Ruby não converte hosts para minúsculas. Um referer ou embed_url como `http://EvilTrout.com/page` portanto falha em host_allowed?, o que bloqueia embedding e recuperação de tópicos, e TopicEmbed.import recorre a nenhuma categoria. Converta ambos os lados da comparação para minúsculas.

suggestions.summary: The 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test passes only because has_topic_embed? is false on an unsaved topic; it does not test the absence of embeddable hosts.
suggestions.content: `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks embeddable hosts. It is now just `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. This test is outside the `with an emeddable host` context, so `has_topic_embed?` is not stubbed. On an unsaved `Fabricate.build(:topic)` it returns false. The test would pass no matter how hosts are handled, so its name says it covers behaviour it does not cover. Either set `embed_truncate = true`, stub `has_topic_embed?` to true and assert the result you actually intend, or rename/remove the test because the host check was intentionally dropped.
suggestions.summaryPt: O teste 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passa apenas porque has_topic_embed? é false em um tópico não salvo; ele não testa a ausência de embeddable hosts.
suggestions.contentPt: `expandable_first_post?` não verifica mais embeddable hosts. Agora é apenas `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. Este teste está fora do contexto `with an emeddable host`, então `has_topic_embed?` não tem stub. Em um `Fabricate.build(:topic)` não salvo, ele retorna false. O teste passaria independentemente de como os hosts são tratados, então seu nome diz cobrir um comportamento que ele não cobre. Defina `embed_truncate = true`, faça stub de `has_topic_embed?` para true e verifique o resultado que você realmente pretende, ou renomeie/remova o teste, já que a verificação de host foi removida intencionalmente.

suggestions.summary: The host lookup lowercases only the stored host, not the incoming referer host, so a referer with uppercase letters never matches its allowed host.
suggestions.content: Only the stored side of the comparison is normalised: `lower(host)` is compared against `uri.host` with its original case. Domains are case-insensitive, so an allowed host gets rejected when the Referer or embed URL has uppercase letters, and TopicEmbed then picks no category. Lowercase both sides, and ideally also lowercase the host when it is saved.
suggestions.summaryPt: A busca de host converte para minúsculas apenas o host armazenado, não o host do referer recebido, então um referer com letras maiúsculas nunca corresponde ao seu host permitido.
suggestions.contentPt: Apenas o lado armazenado da comparação é normalizado: `lower(host)` é comparado com `uri.host` na caixa original. Domínios não diferenciam maiúsculas de minúsculas, então um host permitido é rejeitado quando o Referer ou a URL de embed tem letras maiúsculas, e TopicEmbed então não escolhe nenhuma categoria. Converta ambos os lados para minúsculas e, idealmente, também converta o host para minúsculas ao salvá-lo.

suggestions.summary: `_hydrateEmbedded` now deletes every `*_ids` key and replaces it with possibly-undefined lookups, which breaks existing consumers that read the raw ids.
suggestions.content: Before this change, the regex `/(.+)\_id$/` did not match keys ending in `_ids`, so models kept fields like `group_ids` / `category_ids` exactly as the server sent them. Now any key ending in `_ids` gets `delete obj[k]` unconditionally. Its value moves to `obj[pluralize(subType)]` as the result of `_lookupSubType` for each id, which is `undefined` when the response doesn't sideload that type. Any existing REST-store model or template that reads a raw `*_ids` array loses it. The pluralized property can also overwrite a real field of the same name. To fix: only replace and delete the key when every id resolves (the singular branch already does this with its `if (hydrated)` check), and otherwise leave `obj[k]` as it was.
suggestions.summaryPt: `_hydrateEmbedded` agora remove toda chave `*_ids` e a substitui por lookups possivelmente undefined, o que quebra consumidores existentes que leem os ids brutos.
suggestions.contentPt: Antes desta mudança, o regex `/(.+)\_id$/` não correspondia a chaves terminadas em `_ids`, então os models mantinham campos como `group_ids` / `category_ids` exatamente como o servidor os enviava. Agora qualquer chave terminada em `_ids` recebe `delete obj[k]` incondicionalmente. Seu valor vai para `obj[pluralize(subType)]` como o resultado de `_lookupSubType` para cada id, que é `undefined` quando a resposta não faz sideload desse tipo. Qualquer model ou template do REST store existente que leia um array bruto `*_ids` o perde. A propriedade pluralizada também pode sobrescrever um campo real com o mesmo nome. Para corrigir: só substitua e remova a chave quando todos os ids forem resolvidos (o branch singular já faz isso com sua verificação `if (hydrated)`), e caso contrário deixe `obj[k]` como estava.

suggestions.summary: The migration copies old setting values unchanged, including scheme and path, but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares stored values with a bare uri.host, so migrated URL-style entries never match.
suggestions.content: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting accepted full URLs such as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234`; the old specs used exactly these values. This migration inserts each line as it is, with raw SQL, so the model's `before_validation` normalization never runs. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:10-17) looks up rows with `lower(host) = uri.host`, which assumes stored values are bare, normalized hostnames. Migrated rows that still have a scheme or path will never match. EmbedController will reject those referers and TopicRetriever will treat them as invalid, so embedding breaks on upgraded sites. Normalize each value before inserting: strip whitespace, `sub(/^https?:\/\//,'')`, `sub(/\/.*$/,'')`, and skip blank lines. Escape the value too (for example with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`).
suggestions.summaryPt: A migration copia os valores da configuração antiga sem alteração, incluindo scheme e path, mas EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compara os valores armazenados com um uri.host puro, então entradas migradas em formato de URL nunca correspondem.
suggestions.contentPt: A configuração antiga `embeddable_hosts` aceitava URLs completas como `http://discourse.org` ou `https://example.com/1234`; os specs antigos usavam exatamente esses valores. Esta migration insere cada linha como está, com SQL puro, então a normalização do `before_validation` do model nunca é executada. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:10-17) busca linhas com `lower(host) = uri.host`, o que assume que os valores armazenados são hostnames puros e normalizados. Linhas migradas que ainda têm scheme ou path nunca vão corresponder. O EmbedController rejeitará esses referers e o TopicRetriever os tratará como inválidos, então o embedding quebra em sites atualizados. Normalize cada valor antes de inserir: faça strip de espaços, `sub(/^https?:\/\//,'')`, `sub(/\/.*$/,'')`, e ignore linhas em branco. Escape o valor também (por exemplo com `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`).

suggestions.content: The migration crashes when the `embed_category` row is missing from site_settings, which is the case whenever the setting was left at its default. `execute(...)[0]` is nil, so `['id']` raises NoMethodError. The uncategorized_category_id lookup has the same problem. Hosts are also inserted as raw strings. Values with an http(s):// prefix or a path, which the old setting allowed, are stored as-is and will never match `uri.host` in `record_for_host`, so embedding breaks after the upgrade. A single quote in a value also breaks the INSERT. Fix: check the row count before indexing, strip the scheme and path from each host, and quote values with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.
suggestions.contentPt: A migration quebra quando a linha `embed_category` está ausente em site_settings, o que ocorre sempre que a configuração foi deixada no padrão. `execute(...)[0]` é nil, então `['id']` lança NoMethodError. A busca de uncategorized_category_id tem o mesmo problema. Os hosts também são inseridos como strings brutas. Valores com prefixo http(s):// ou um path, que a configuração antiga permitia, são armazenados como estão e nunca vão corresponder a `uri.host` em `record_for_host`, então o embedding quebra após o upgrade. Uma aspa simples em um valor também quebra o INSERT. Correção: verifique a contagem de linhas antes de acessar o índice, remova scheme e path de cada host, e escape os valores com `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.

suggestions.content: The before_validation callback calls `self.host.sub!` without checking for nil. Saving through the admin controller without a host param, or validating `EmbeddableHost.new`, raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard it with `if self.host.present?` (or use safe navigation) and add `validates :host, presence: true`.
suggestions.contentPt: O callback before_validation chama `self.host.sub!` sem verificar nil. Salvar pelo controller de admin sem o param host, ou validar `EmbeddableHost.new`, lança NoMethodError em vez de retornar um erro de validação. Proteja com `if self.host.present?` (ou use safe navigation) e adicione `validates :host, presence: true`.

suggestions.content: The plural branch runs on every key ending in `_ids`. It calls `obj[k].map` without a null check, so a null value throws. It also always deletes the original id array, even when `_lookupSubType` finds no matching collection in the root and returns undefined for every id. Any rest-serialized payload with a plain id array (e.g. `user_ids`) therefore loses its ids and gets an array of undefined instead. Only replace and delete the key when `obj[k]` is an array and the plural collection exists in the root.
suggestions.contentPt: O branch plural roda em toda chave terminada em `_ids`. Ele chama `obj[k].map` sem null check, então um valor null lança erro. Também sempre remove o array de ids original, mesmo quando `_lookupSubType` não encontra coleção correspondente no root e retorna undefined para cada id. Qualquer payload serializado pelo rest com um array simples de ids (ex.: `user_ids`) portanto perde seus ids e recebe um array de undefined. Só substitua e remova a chave quando `obj[k]` for um array e a coleção plural existir no root.

suggestions.content: `update` and `destroy` call methods on `EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first` without checking for nil. An unknown or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404. Use `find` (raises RecordNotFound, which is handled) or add an explicit nil check.
suggestions.contentPt: `update` e `destroy` chamam métodos em `EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first` sem verificar nil. Um id desconhecido ou já excluído lança NoMethodError e retorna 500 em vez de 404. Use `find` (lança RecordNotFound, que é tratado) ou adicione uma verificação explícita de nil.

suggestions.content: The fabricator file contents are swapped. embeddable_host_fabricator.rb now holds the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators, and category_fabricator.rb (lines 1-4) holds only :embeddable_host. Each file name now describes the other file's contents, so anyone looking for the category fabricators in category_fabricator.rb will not find them. Fix: restore the category fabricators to category_fabricator.rb and put the :embeddable_host fabricator in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.
suggestions.contentPt: O conteúdo dos arquivos de fabricator está trocado. embeddable_host_fabricator.rb agora contém os fabricators :category, :diff_category, :happy_category e :private_category, e category_fabricator.rb (linhas 1-4) contém apenas :embeddable_host. Cada nome de arquivo agora descreve o conteúdo do outro arquivo, então quem procurar os fabricators de categoria em category_fabricator.rb não os encontrará. Correção: restaure os fabricators de categoria em category_fabricator.rb e coloque o fabricator :embeddable_host em embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

suggestions.content: The test name 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' is no longer accurate. This PR removed the host check from Topic#expandable_first_post?, which now checks only embed_truncate? and has_topic_embed?. The test passes only because has_topic_embed? is false on an unsaved topic. Fix: rename it to describe what actually makes the result false (for example 'is false without a topic embed'), or remove it.
suggestions.contentPt: O nome do teste 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' não está mais correto. Este PR removeu a verificação de host de Topic#expandable_first_post?, que agora verifica apenas embed_truncate? e has_topic_embed?. O teste passa apenas porque has_topic_embed? é false em um tópico não salvo. Correção: renomeie-o para descrever o que realmente torna o resultado false (por exemplo 'is false without a topic embed'), ou remova-o.

suggestions.content: The describe block 'allows_embeddable_host' uses the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? name, but its tests exercise EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?. Fix: rename the block to 'host_allowed?' so it matches the method under test.
suggestions.contentPt: O bloco describe 'allows_embeddable_host' usa o nome removido SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?, mas seus testes exercitam EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?. Correção: renomeie o bloco para 'host_allowed?' para que corresponda ao método testado.

The _ids branch of _hydrateEmbedded deletes raw id arrays even when nothing resolves, leaving arrays of undefined and possibly overwriting a field. It also calls .map on a possible null, and its `|| []` guard is dead code.

suggestions.content: WHAT: The async legacy writes in Create (line 51), Delete (line 110), Update (line 135) and DeleteCollection (line 163) get their timeout context from the request ctx, which the apiserver cancels as soon as the handler returns. WHY: Usually the legacy write is cancelled right after the response is sent, so the legacy store silently stops getting creates, updates and deletes and falls out of sync, which defeats the 'safe measure' purpose of mode 3. Legacy errors are also never logged, only counted in metrics. HOW: Use `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 10*time.Second, ...)` so values such as the identity are kept but the request's cancellation is not, and call `log.Error` when the legacy call fails.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: As escritas legacy assíncronas em Create (linha 51), Delete (linha 110), Update (linha 135) e DeleteCollection (linha 163) obtêm o context de timeout a partir do ctx da requisição, que o apiserver cancela assim que o handler retorna. POR QUÊ: Normalmente a escrita legacy é cancelada logo depois de a resposta ser enviada, então o legacy store silenciosamente deixa de receber creates, updates e deletes e sai de sincronia, o que anula o propósito de 'medida de segurança' do mode 3. Além disso, os erros do legacy nunca são logados, apenas contados em métricas. CORREÇÃO: Use `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 10*time.Second, ...)` para que valores como a identidade sejam mantidos, mas o cancelamento da requisição não, e chame `log.Error` quando a chamada ao legacy falhar.

suggestions.content: WHAT: Legacy Update now gets the caller's original objInfo instead of the earlier updateWrapper that carried the object Unified Storage produced. WHY: Legacy recomputes the update (patch, preconditions, resourceVersion) against its own old copy, so the update can fail on a resourceVersion or precondition mismatch, or produce a different object from Unified Storage. The stores then diverge with no log. HOW: Wrap the result as before: `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res}`.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: O Update do legacy agora recebe o objInfo original do chamador, em vez do updateWrapper anterior que carregava o objeto produzido pelo Unified Storage. POR QUÊ: O legacy recalcula o update (patch, preconditions, resourceVersion) contra sua própria cópia antiga, então o update pode falhar por divergência de resourceVersion ou de precondition, ou produzir um objeto diferente do Unified Storage. Os stores então divergem sem nenhum log. CORREÇÃO: Envolva o resultado como antes: `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res}`.

suggestions.content: WHAT: Metrics are recorded with the wrong helper or the wrong label. Create (line 45) and Update (line 129) report a Unified Storage failure through recordLegacyDuration. Delete success (line 106) passes `name` instead of `options.Kind` as the kind label. The DeleteCollection goroutine (line 166) records the legacy call with recordStorageDuration. Delete (line 97) also puts d.Log into the ctx instead of the enriched `log`. WHY: Storage errors show up as legacy errors, legacy delete-collection latency is counted as storage, and putting object names in a label creates unbounded label cardinality. Together these make the dual-writer dashboards misleading. HOW: Use recordStorageDuration at lines 45 and 129, options.Kind at line 106, recordLegacyDuration at line 166, and `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)` at line 97.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: As métricas são registradas com o helper errado ou o label errado. Create (linha 45) e Update (linha 129) reportam uma falha do Unified Storage através de recordLegacyDuration. O sucesso do Delete (linha 106) passa `name` em vez de `options.Kind` como label de kind. A goroutine de DeleteCollection (linha 166) registra a chamada legacy com recordStorageDuration. O Delete (linha 97) também coloca d.Log no ctx em vez do `log` enriquecido. POR QUÊ: Erros de storage aparecem como erros de legacy, a latência de delete-collection do legacy é contada como storage, e colocar nomes de objetos em um label cria cardinalidade ilimitada de labels. Juntos, esses problemas tornam os dashboards do dual-writer enganosos. CORREÇÃO: Use recordStorageDuration nas linhas 45 e 129, options.Kind na linha 106, recordLegacyDuration na linha 166 e `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)` na linha 97.

suggestions.content: WHAT: The goroutine passes the same `obj` pointer to Legacy.Create after Storage.Create has already used it. Storage.Create may have mutated it (UID, resourceVersion), and it may be the same object that the handler is serializing concurrently. WHY: Legacy can receive Unified Storage metadata, and concurrent access to the object can cause a data race. HOW: Pass `obj.DeepCopyObject()` into the goroutine.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: A goroutine passa o mesmo ponteiro `obj` para Legacy.Create depois que Storage.Create já o utilizou. Storage.Create pode tê-lo mutado (UID, resourceVersion), e ele pode ser o mesmo objeto que o handler está serializando concorrentemente. POR QUÊ: O Legacy pode receber metadados do Unified Storage, e o acesso concorrente ao objeto pode causar uma data race. CORREÇÃO: Passe `obj.DeepCopyObject()` para a goroutine.

suggestions.summary: Legacy writes now run in unordered goroutines, so writes to the same object can reach legacy storage in a different order than the client sent them.
suggestions.content: Mode 3 now starts each legacy write (Create, Update, Delete, DeleteCollection) in its own goroutine and returns at once. Nothing keeps those writes in the order the client sent them. Example: a client creates X and gets a response, then deletes X. If the legacy Delete goroutine runs before the legacy Create goroutine, the delete fails with NotFound, the create then succeeds, and X stays in legacy storage even though it was deleted. Two updates in a row can likewise leave legacy with an older version. Either keep the legacy write synchronous, as before this PR, or send legacy writes through a per-object (or per-resource) queue or lock so they run in the order they were issued.
suggestions.summaryPt: As escritas legacy agora rodam em goroutines sem ordenação, então escritas no mesmo objeto podem chegar ao legacy storage em ordem diferente da enviada pelo cliente.
suggestions.contentPt: O Mode 3 agora inicia cada escrita legacy (Create, Update, Delete, DeleteCollection) em sua própria goroutine e retorna imediatamente. Nada mantém essas escritas na ordem em que o cliente as enviou. Exemplo: um cliente cria X e recebe uma resposta, depois deleta X. Se a goroutine do Delete legacy rodar antes da goroutine do Create legacy, o delete falha com NotFound, o create então tem sucesso, e X permanece no legacy storage mesmo tendo sido deletado. Dois updates seguidos também podem deixar o legacy com uma versão mais antiga. Mantenha a escrita legacy síncrona, como era antes deste PR, ou envie as escritas legacy por uma fila ou lock por objeto (ou por resource) para que rodem na ordem em que foram emitidas.

suggestions.summary: Delete passes the resource name instead of the kind as the metric label to recordStorageDuration, causing incorrect labels and high cardinality.
suggestions.content: In Delete, the resource `name` is passed as the kind label to `recordStorageDuration`. This puts individual resource names into a Prometheus label, which makes the label incorrect (it should be the kind) and creates a cardinality problem. The reviewer noted it is not a sensitive-data exposure, so it was outside their data-exposure assignment.
suggestions.summaryPt: Delete passa o nome do resource em vez do kind como label da métrica para recordStorageDuration, causando labels incorretos e alta cardinalidade.
suggestions.contentPt: Em Delete, o `name` do resource é passado como label de kind para `recordStorageDuration`. Isso coloca nomes individuais de resources em um label do Prometheus, o que torna o label incorreto (deveria ser o kind) e cria um problema de cardinalidade. O revisor observou que isso não é uma exposição de dados sensíveis, portanto estava fora da sua atribuição de exposição de dados.

suggestions.summary: Delete stores d.Log in the context instead of the enriched logger, so downstream logs lose contextual fields.
suggestions.content: Delete puts the base `d.Log` logger into the context instead of the enriched logger. Downstream logging loses the contextual fields such as kind, name, method and mode. It does not expose any sensitive data.
suggestions.summaryPt: Delete armazena d.Log no context em vez do logger enriquecido, então os logs downstream perdem campos contextuais.
suggestions.contentPt: Delete coloca o logger base `d.Log` no context em vez do logger enriquecido. O logging downstream perde os campos contextuais como kind, name, method e mode. Isso não expõe nenhum dado sensível.

suggestions.summary: Create failure in unified storage is recorded as legacy duration.
suggestions.content: When d.Storage.Create fails, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) with startStorage. That times the unified-storage call but adds it to the legacy histogram, so storage error metrics undercount and legacy metrics get bogus errors. Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).
suggestions.summaryPt: A falha de Create no unified storage é registrada como duração de legacy.
suggestions.contentPt: Quando d.Storage.Create falha, o código chama d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) com startStorage. Isso mede o tempo da chamada ao unified-storage, mas o adiciona ao histograma de legacy, de modo que as métricas de erro de storage ficam subcontadas e as métricas de legacy recebem erros falsos. Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

suggestions.summary: Update failure in unified storage is recorded as legacy duration.
suggestions.content: When d.Storage.Update fails, the timing is sent to recordLegacyDuration even though the measured operation was the storage update. Use recordStorageDuration. The same mix-up happens in reverse at line 166: the legacy DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration with startLegacy, but it should call recordLegacyDuration.
suggestions.summaryPt: A falha de Update no unified storage é registrada como duração de legacy.
suggestions.contentPt: Quando d.Storage.Update falha, a medição de tempo é enviada para recordLegacyDuration, embora a operação medida tenha sido o update do storage. Use recordStorageDuration. A mesma confusão acontece no sentido inverso na linha 166: a goroutine de DeleteCollection do legacy chama recordStorageDuration com startLegacy, mas deveria chamar recordLegacyDuration.

suggestions.summary: Delete success metric is labeled with the object name instead of the kind.
suggestions.content: Every other call passes options.Kind as the metric's name label, but the Delete success path passes `name` (the object name). This puts per-object values into the label, which can blow up label cardinality, and it breaks consistency with the error path at line 103 and the legacy path at line 113.
suggestions.summaryPt: A métrica de sucesso do Delete é rotulada com o nome do objeto em vez do kind.
suggestions.contentPt: Todas as outras chamadas passam options.Kind como label name da métrica, mas o caminho de sucesso do Delete passa `name` (o nome do objeto). Isso coloca valores por objeto no label, o que pode explodir a cardinalidade de labels, e quebra a consistência com o caminho de erro na linha 103 e com o caminho legacy na linha 113.

suggestions.summary: Delete stores the base logger in the context instead of the enriched `log`.
suggestions.content: Delete builds `log` with the name, kind and method values, but then calls klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log). Downstream storage code that reads the logger from the context therefore does not get those values. Every other method passes `log`.
suggestions.summaryPt: Delete armazena o logger base no context em vez do `log` enriquecido.
suggestions.contentPt: Delete constrói `log` com os valores de name, kind e method, mas depois chama klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log). O código de storage downstream que lê o logger do context, portanto, não recebe esses valores. Todos os outros métodos passam `log`.

suggestions.summary: Mode3 writes to legacy storage in a background goroutine tied to the request context, but the new Mode3 playlist integration tests read the legacy API immediately and expect it to match.
suggestions.content: In Mode3, Create, Update (lines 134-141), Delete (108-114) and DeleteCollection (161-167) now write to legacy storage in a goroutine and return without waiting. That goroutine uses a context derived from the request, so the legacy write can be cancelled once the response is sent. The new Mode3 integration tests in pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go (lines 132-204) run doPlaylistTests. That suite creates and updates through k8s, then immediately reads `/api/playlists` and expects the same result. Because nothing guarantees the legacy write has finished (or succeeded), those tests are racy and legacy data can silently diverge. Fix: run the legacy write on a detached context (e.g. `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`). Then either make the tests poll or wait until legacy catches up, or keep the legacy write synchronous until the tests are changed to accept eventual consistency.
suggestions.summaryPt: O Mode3 escreve no legacy storage em uma goroutine em background atrelada ao context da requisição, mas os novos testes de integração de playlist do Mode3 leem a API legacy imediatamente e esperam que ela coincida.
suggestions.contentPt: No Mode3, Create, Update (linhas 134-141), Delete (108-114) e DeleteCollection (161-167) agora escrevem no legacy storage em uma goroutine e retornam sem esperar. Essa goroutine usa um context derivado da requisição, então a escrita legacy pode ser cancelada depois que a resposta for enviada. Os novos testes de integração do Mode3 em pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go (linhas 132-204) executam doPlaylistTests. Essa suíte cria e atualiza via k8s, depois lê imediatamente `/api/playlists` e espera o mesmo resultado. Como nada garante que a escrita legacy tenha terminado (ou tido sucesso), esses testes são racy e os dados do legacy podem divergir silenciosamente. Correção: execute a escrita legacy em um context desacoplado (ex.: `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`). Depois, faça os testes fazerem polling ou esperarem até o legacy alcançar, ou mantenha a escrita legacy síncrona até os testes serem alterados para aceitar consistência eventual.

suggestions.content: The background legacy writes in Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection (lines 50-57, 108-114, 134-141, 161-167) build their timeout context from the request `ctx`. The apiserver cancels that context soon after the handler returns. So the 10s timeout gives no protection: the legacy Create/Update/Delete is often cancelled partway through or before it starts. Unified storage has already committed by then, so the legacy store silently diverges from it. Derive the context with `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), ...)` to keep request values but drop the parent's cancellation.
suggestions.contentPt: As escritas legacy em background em Create, Delete, Update e DeleteCollection (linhas 50-57, 108-114, 134-141, 161-167) constroem seu context de timeout a partir do `ctx` da requisição. O apiserver cancela esse context logo depois que o handler retorna. Assim, o timeout de 10s não oferece proteção: o Create/Update/Delete legacy é frequentemente cancelado no meio ou antes de começar. O unified storage já fez o commit nesse momento, então o legacy store silenciosamente diverge dele. Derive o context com `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), ...)` para manter os valores da requisição, mas descartar o cancelamento do pai.

suggestions.content: Update used to wrap objInfo in `updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}`, so legacy stored exactly the object that unified storage produced. Mode1 and mode2 still do this. Now the raw objInfo goes to Legacy.Update, which re-applies the patch or transform to legacy's own current object, and does so asynchronously. If an earlier async write hasn't landed yet or legacy has drifted, the two stores end up with different contents. Pass `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res}` to Legacy.Update.
suggestions.contentPt: O Update costumava envolver o objInfo em `updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}`, de modo que o legacy armazenava exatamente o objeto produzido pelo unified storage. Mode1 e mode2 ainda fazem isso. Agora o objInfo bruto vai para Legacy.Update, que reaplica o patch ou a transformação ao objeto atual do próprio legacy, e o faz de forma assíncrona. Se uma escrita assíncrona anterior ainda não foi concluída ou se o legacy divergiu, os dois stores acabam com conteúdos diferentes. Passe `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res}` para Legacy.Update.

suggestions.content: This is a data race. In Create, `obj` (which Storage.Create may have mutated, or which may be the same pointer as `created`) goes to Legacy.Create in a goroutine while the same object is returned to the caller. The legacy store can mutate metadata such as resourceVersion, uid and annotations while the response encoder is serializing `created`. That can corrupt the response or panic on a concurrent map access. Give the goroutine its own copy with obj.DeepCopyObject().
suggestions.contentPt: Isto é uma data race. Em Create, `obj` (que Storage.Create pode ter mutado, ou que pode ser o mesmo ponteiro que `created`) vai para Legacy.Create em uma goroutine enquanto o mesmo objeto é retornado ao chamador. O legacy store pode mutar metadados como resourceVersion, uid e annotations enquanto o encoder da resposta serializa `created`. Isso pode corromper a resposta ou causar panic por acesso concorrente a um map. Dê à goroutine sua própria cópia com obj.DeepCopyObject().

suggestions.summary: The 'unified store fails' Create case only sets up the legacy mock, and because the mock is shared, that legacy expectation is what makes the storage call fail.
suggestions.content: Case 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' only registers a Create expectation in setupLegacyFn and has no setupStorageFn. legacyStoreMock and storageMock wrap the same *mock.Mock `m` (storage_mocks_test.go:14-19, 32, 96), so DualWriterMode3.Create's Storage.Create call (dualwriter_mode3.go:42) is answered by the expectation meant for the legacy store. The test would still pass if mode 3 read from legacy instead of storage. Fix: use separate mocks for each store and put the failing expectation in setupStorageFn.
suggestions.summaryPt: O caso de Create 'unified store fails' só configura o mock do legacy, e como o mock é compartilhado, é essa expectativa do legacy que faz a chamada ao storage falhar.
suggestions.contentPt: O caso 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' registra apenas uma expectativa de Create em setupLegacyFn e não tem setupStorageFn. legacyStoreMock e storageMock envolvem o mesmo *mock.Mock `m` (storage_mocks_test.go:14-19, 32, 96), então a chamada Storage.Create de DualWriterMode3.Create (dualwriter_mode3.go:42) é respondida pela expectativa destinada ao legacy store. O teste ainda passaria se o mode 3 lesse do legacy em vez do storage. Correção: use mocks separados para cada store e coloque a expectativa de falha em setupStorageFn.

suggestions.summary: The mode-3 write tests never check the asynchronous legacy write, so they still pass with the legacy writes removed.
suggestions.content: Mode 3 is defined as writing to both stores, but Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection now do the legacy write in a goroutine (dualwriter_mode3.go:50-57, 108-114, 134-141, 161-167). The tests return right after the storage call. They never call AssertExpectations and never wait for the goroutine. The Delete and DeleteCollection cases don't set up a legacy expectation at all, so the goroutine hits an unexpected mock call that can panic or be lost depending on timing. Removing the legacy writes would leave every test green. Fix: use separate legacy mocks, wait on a condition (for example, assert.Eventually on legacy AssertCalled), and assert that the legacy call happened.
suggestions.summaryPt: Os testes de escrita do mode 3 nunca verificam a escrita legacy assíncrona, então continuam passando mesmo com as escritas legacy removidas.
suggestions.contentPt: O Mode 3 é definido como escrita em ambos os stores, mas Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection agora fazem a escrita legacy em uma goroutine (dualwriter_mode3.go:50-57, 108-114, 134-141, 161-167). Os testes retornam logo após a chamada ao storage. Eles nunca chamam AssertExpectations e nunca esperam pela goroutine. Os casos de Delete e DeleteCollection nem configuram uma expectativa do legacy, então a goroutine atinge uma chamada de mock inesperada que pode causar panic ou se perder dependendo do timing. Remover as escritas legacy deixaria todos os testes verdes. Correção: use mocks legacy separados, espere por uma condição (por exemplo, assert.Eventually em AssertCalled do legacy) e verifique que a chamada ao legacy aconteceu.

suggestions.content: Delete used to tolerate `apierrors.IsNotFound` from Storage.Delete and still delete from legacy (also ignoring NotFound there). Now any storage error, NotFound included, is returned right away and the legacy delete is skipped. In mode 3, an object written before the switch exists only in legacy storage. Deleting it now fails with 404 and the legacy copy stays behind. Bring back the NotFound fallback: on NotFound, still delete from legacy and only return the error if the legacy delete also fails. Mode2 keeps NotFound checks (dualwriter_mode2.go:246/257).
suggestions.contentPt: O Delete costumava tolerar `apierrors.IsNotFound` vindo de Storage.Delete e ainda deletava do legacy (ignorando NotFound lá também). Agora qualquer erro de storage, NotFound inclusive, é retornado imediatamente e o delete do legacy é pulado. No mode 3, um objeto escrito antes da troca existe apenas no legacy storage. Deletá-lo agora falha com 404 e a cópia legacy permanece. Restaure o fallback de NotFound: em NotFound, ainda delete do legacy e só retorne o erro se o delete do legacy também falhar. O Mode2 mantém as verificações de NotFound (dualwriter_mode2.go:246/257).

suggestions.content: The old Update passed `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}` to Legacy.Update, so legacy got exactly the object that unified storage had stored. The new code passes the raw `objInfo`, so legacy re-runs UpdatedObject against its own copy. That copy can have a different resourceVersion or old state, so legacy can now reject the update (conflict or precondition failure) or store a different object, and the stores drift apart. Mode1 and mode2 still wrap the update (dualwriter_mode2.go:298, dualwriter_mode1.go:250). Wrap `res` from Storage.Update in updateWrapper before calling Legacy.Update.
suggestions.contentPt: O Update antigo passava `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}` para Legacy.Update, então o legacy recebia exatamente o objeto que o unified storage havia armazenado. O novo código passa o `objInfo` bruto, então o legacy reexecuta UpdatedObject contra sua própria cópia. Essa cópia pode ter um resourceVersion diferente ou estado antigo, então o legacy agora pode rejeitar o update (conflito ou falha de precondition) ou armazenar um objeto diferente, e os stores divergem. Mode1 e mode2 ainda envolvem o update (dualwriter_mode2.go:298, dualwriter_mode1.go:250). Envolva o `res` de Storage.Update em updateWrapper antes de chamar Legacy.Update.

suggestions.content: Legacy writes used to run synchronously within the request. They now run in a goroutine whose context comes from the request `ctx`. The API server cancels that ctx when the handler returns, so the legacy Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection calls can be cancelled before they finish. Failures are not logged either: only a metric is recorded. Code that relies on the legacy store being written in mode 3, such as the new playlist mode 3 tests or a rollback to mode 1/2, loses that guarantee. Start the goroutine from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` and log any legacy error. This applies to lines 108-114, 134-141 and 161-167 as well.
suggestions.contentPt: As escritas legacy costumavam rodar de forma síncrona dentro da requisição. Agora rodam em uma goroutine cujo context vem do `ctx` da requisição. O API server cancela esse ctx quando o handler retorna, então as chamadas Create, Update, Delete e DeleteCollection do legacy podem ser canceladas antes de terminar. As falhas também não são logadas: apenas uma métrica é registrada. Código que depende de o legacy store ser escrito no mode 3, como os novos testes de playlist do mode 3 ou um rollback para mode 1/2, perde essa garantia. Inicie a goroutine a partir de `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` e logue qualquer erro do legacy. Isto também se aplica às linhas 108-114, 134-141 e 161-167.

suggestions.summary: Test name says List is 'not implemented', but this PR implements List and the case tests a storage error.
suggestions.content: This test name says List is not implemented in the unified store. This PR removed the `List not implemented` stub and added a real List that calls `d.Storage.List` (dualwriter_mode3.go:79-92). The case only checks that a mocked storage error is returned. If this test fails, the name will point readers to a problem that no longer exists. Rename it to match what it checks, e.g. "error when listing an object in the unified store fails".
suggestions.summaryPt: O nome do teste diz que List 'não está implementado', mas este PR implementa List e o caso testa um erro de storage.
suggestions.contentPt: O nome deste teste diz que List não está implementado no unified store. Este PR removeu o stub `List not implemented` e adicionou um List real que chama `d.Storage.List` (dualwriter_mode3.go:79-92). O caso apenas verifica que um erro de storage mockado é retornado. Se este teste falhar, o nome apontará os leitores para um problema que não existe mais. Renomeie-o para corresponder ao que ele verifica, ex.: "error when listing an object in the unified store fails".

groups.defect: The async legacy writes in Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection take their timeout context from the request ctx, which is cancelled when the handler returns, so legacy writes get cancelled and the stores diverge. Legacy errors are also never logged, and the new mode-3 playlist integration tests that read legacy right away are racy.
Create (line 45) and Update (line 129) record storage failures with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration (dualwriter_mode3.go).
Delete success path passes name instead of options.Kind as the kind label of recordStorageDuration (dualwriter_mode3.go:106).
Delete puts d.Log into the context instead of the enriched log (dualwriter_mode3.go:97).
Legacy Update gets the raw objInfo instead of an updateWrapper around the object that unified storage produced, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge or fail.

In DualWriterMode3.Create, the goroutine passes the same `obj` pointer to Legacy.Create after Storage.Create has used it, while that object may also be returned or serialized. This allows concurrent mutation and a data race. The fix is to pass obj.DeepCopyObject() into the goroutine.
groups.arbiterReasoning: Both suggestions point at the same code: Create, line 55, inside the 42-59 range. They report the same defect. The shared `obj` pointer, which Storage.Create may have changed, goes to Legacy.Create in a goroutine while the caller may be serializing the same object. Both propose the same fix, DeepCopyObject. The judges disagreed only on needsUnifiedComment. s_4ee7f335 adds that Unified Storage metadata could reach Legacy. That is another consequence of the same shared or mutated pointer, and the same single edit at the same place fixes it. It is not a separate defect needing its own fix, so one member's comment covers the group. needsUnifiedComment is false.

groups.defect: The async legacy writes in Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection take their timeout context from the request ctx, which is cancelled when the handler returns, so legacy writes get cancelled and the stores diverge. Legacy errors are also never logged, and the new mode-3 playlist integration tests that read legacy right away are racy.
groups.rationale: All four report the same request-context cancellation problem in the background legacy goroutines, with the same WithoutCancel fix. Some members also mention the missing error logging and the racy integration tests.

groups.defect: Metrics are recorded with the wrong helper or label: Create (line 45) and Update (line 129) send storage failures to recordLegacyDuration, the legacy DeleteCollection call (line 166) uses recordStorageDuration, and the Delete success path (line 106) passes name instead of kind. Delete (line 97) also puts d.Log into the context instead of the enriched log.
groups.rationale: s_74e86eb7 reports all of these mix-ups, including the Delete logger. Each other member reports one or more of them, so the overlap chain links them into one group.

groups.defect: Legacy Update gets the raw objInfo instead of an updateWrapper around the object that unified storage produced, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge or fail.
groups.rationale: All three point at the same lines with the same missing updateWrapper and the same fix.

groups.defect: The Create goroutine passes the shared obj pointer to Legacy.Create while the same object may be mutated or serialized elsewhere, causing a data race. Fix: use DeepCopyObject.
groups.rationale: Both report the same shared-object data race in Create and propose the same deep-copy fix.

groups.defect: Legacy.Update receives raw objInfo instead of an updateWrapper containing the unified-storage result, allowing recomputation against different legacy state.
groups.rationale: All three report the same removed wrapper and resulting divergence. Restoring the wrapper at the legacy update call addresses all three.

groups.defect: Create and Update storage failures use the legacy metric helper, legacy DeleteCollection uses the storage metric helper, successful Delete labels metrics with the object name, and Delete installs the unenriched logger in its context.
groups.rationale: s_74e86eb7 explicitly reports every defect covered by the other members, connecting them through overlap. The merged comment must retain the repeated metric attribution mistakes and the separate label and logger corrections.

groups.defect: All four asynchronous legacy write paths inherit request cancellation; legacy failures are no longer logged, and the playlist integration tests immediately assert legacy consistency without waiting for replication.
groups.rationale: Every member reports request cancellation reaching background legacy writes. s_03fc7aa9 and s_ffe2609d additionally report missing error logs, while s_f50f8610 adds the integration-test race, so all must survive consolidation.

groups.defect: Create shares a mutable object with the legacy goroutine and response handling, risking concurrent mutation during serialization and passing unified-storage metadata to legacy.
groups.rationale: Both report the same shared-object race at Legacy.Create. s_4ee7f335 additionally identifies unified-storage metadata reaching legacy as a problem.

suggestions.content: WHAT: The null check labeled 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`. WHY: A null rawTokenId gets through, and encodeTokenId then builds a jti like `onrtac:null` instead of failing fast. HOW: Change line 73 to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: O null check com o rótulo 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' verifica `grantType` novamente em vez de `rawTokenId`. POR QUÊ: Um rawTokenId nulo passa, e encodeTokenId então monta um jti como `onrtac:null` em vez de falhar imediatamente. CORREÇÃO: Altere a linha 73 para `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

suggestions.content: WHAT: isAccessTokenId reads `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, but the encoder puts the grant shortcut at characters 4-6 (sessionType 0-2, tokenType 2-4, grant 4-6). The check also returns false when the shortcut matches, which is inverted. WHY: The matcher never checks the grant type. A token with the wrong grant shortcut still passes, and a correct one passes only because the wrong substring never equals the shortcut. So the event assertions in expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken give no regression coverage. HOW: `if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: isAccessTokenId lê `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, mas o encoder coloca o shortcut do grant nos caracteres 4-6 (sessionType 0-2, tokenType 2-4, grant 4-6). A verificação também retorna false quando o shortcut coincide, o que está invertido. POR QUÊ: O matcher nunca verifica o grant type. Um token com o shortcut de grant errado ainda passa, e um correto só passa porque a substring errada nunca é igual ao shortcut. Assim, as asserções de eventos em expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken e expectAuthReqIdToToken não dão nenhuma cobertura contra regressões. CORREÇÃO: `if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

suggestions.content: WHAT: `getShortcut()` is a new abstract SPI method with no default. Its contract says 'usually like 3-letters', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId requires the encoded context to be exactly 6 chars (2+2+2). Nothing validates the shortcut's length or non-null value. WHY: Existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations no longer compile, or hit AbstractMethodError at runtime. A custom shortcut that is not 2 chars produces access-token IDs that the decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException. A null shortcut makes `grantsByShortcuts.put(null, ...)` in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit throw an NPE, because ConcurrentHashMap rejects null keys, and server startup fails. HOW: Document and enforce a 2-character, non-null shortcut (validate it in postInit and in getShortcutByGrantType). Consider a default implementation so existing providers still compile.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: `getShortcut()` é um novo método abstrato de SPI sem implementação default. Seu contrato diz 'usually like 3-letters', mas DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId exige que o contexto codificado tenha exatamente 6 caracteres (2+2+2). Nada valida o tamanho do shortcut nem se ele é não nulo. POR QUÊ: Implementações customizadas existentes de OAuth2GrantTypeFactory deixam de compilar ou sofrem AbstractMethodError em runtime. Um shortcut customizado que não tenha 2 caracteres gera IDs de access token que o decoder rejeita com IllegalArgumentException. Um shortcut nulo faz `grantsByShortcuts.put(null, ...)` em DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit lançar um NPE, porque ConcurrentHashMap rejeita chaves nulas, e a inicialização do servidor falha. CORREÇÃO: Documente e imponha um shortcut não nulo de 2 caracteres (valide em postInit e em getShortcutByGrantType). Considere uma implementação default para que os providers existentes continuem compilando.

suggestions.summary: The isAccessTokenId matcher reads the wrong 2 characters (substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6)) and its comparison is inverted, so it never checks the grant type.
suggestions.content: The encoder writes the token ID prefix as sessionType(0-2) + tokenType(2-4) + grantShortcut(4-6). For the prefix "onrtac", substring(3,5) gives "ta", which mixes the token-type and grant characters. On top of that, the check returns false when the segment *equals* the expected shortcut. So in practice the matcher accepts any well-formed ID with any grant type, and the new test assertions in expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken check nothing about the grant. Use substring(4,6) and return false when the segment does *not* equal the expected shortcut.
suggestions.summaryPt: O matcher isAccessTokenId lê os 2 caracteres errados (substring(3,5) em vez de substring(4,6)) e sua comparação está invertida, então nunca verifica o grant type.
suggestions.contentPt: O encoder escreve o prefixo do token ID como sessionType(0-2) + tokenType(2-4) + grantShortcut(4-6). Para o prefixo "onrtac", substring(3,5) resulta em "ta", que mistura os caracteres de token type e de grant. Além disso, a verificação retorna false quando o segmento *é igual* ao shortcut esperado. Na prática, o matcher aceita qualquer ID bem formado com qualquer grant type, e as novas asserções de teste em expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken e expectAuthReqIdToToken não verificam nada sobre o grant. Use substring(4,6) e retorne false quando o segmento *não for igual* ao shortcut esperado.

suggestions.summary: The isAccessTokenId matcher reads the wrong substring and inverts the comparison, so it never checks the grant shortcut.
suggestions.content: The grant shortcut is the 5th-6th characters of the 6-character prefix, so it is `substring(4, 6)`, but the matcher uses `substring(3, 5)`. It also returns false when the slice *matches* the expected shortcut instead of when it differs. As a result, token IDs with any grant (including "na" when the GRANT_TYPE attribute is never set) pass `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, the device-code check and the CIBA check. Fix: check `items[0].length() == 6` and `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.
suggestions.summaryPt: O matcher isAccessTokenId lê a substring errada e inverte a comparação, então nunca verifica o shortcut do grant.
suggestions.contentPt: O shortcut do grant são o 5º e o 6º caracteres do prefixo de 6 caracteres, portanto é `substring(4, 6)`, mas o matcher usa `substring(3, 5)`. Ele também retorna false quando o trecho *coincide* com o shortcut esperado, em vez de quando difere. Como resultado, token IDs com qualquer grant (incluindo "na" quando o atributo GRANT_TYPE nunca é definido) passam em `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, na verificação de device-code e na verificação de CIBA. Correção: verifique `items[0].length() == 6` e `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

suggestions.summary: testIncorrectGrantType passes on a NullPointerException from the null sessionFactory, not on the grant-type validation.
suggestions.content: In this fixture `factory.sessionFactory` is null because `postInit` is never called. For the unmapped shortcut "ac", `getGrantTypeByShortcut` calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws a NullPointerException. The test catches any RuntimeException, so it passes without ever reaching the `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type")` branch, and would still pass if that validation were removed. Fix: give the factory a stub sessionFactory that returns an empty stream, and catch IllegalArgumentException specifically (ideally also asserting on the message).
suggestions.summaryPt: testIncorrectGrantType passa por causa de uma NullPointerException do sessionFactory nulo, e não pela validação do grant-type.
suggestions.contentPt: Neste fixture, `factory.sessionFactory` é null porque `postInit` nunca é chamado. Para o shortcut não mapeado "ac", `getGrantTypeByShortcut` chama `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` e lança uma NullPointerException. O teste captura qualquer RuntimeException, então passa sem nunca chegar ao branch `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type")`, e continuaria passando mesmo se essa validação fosse removida. Correção: forneça à factory um stub de sessionFactory que retorne um stream vazio, e capture especificamente IllegalArgumentException (idealmente também verificando a mensagem).

suggestions.summary: This null check is on grantType, but its message says rawTokenId.

suggestions.summary: The getShortcut() javadoc suggests 3-letter shortcuts, but the encoder only accepts exactly 2 characters.
suggestions.content: The javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters". DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId requires the encoded prefix to be exactly 6 chars and reads the grant shortcut as chars 4-6. A custom grant written to follow this javadoc, with a 3-letter shortcut, would produce token IDs that fail to decode with "Expected length of 6". The doc should say the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters.

suggestions.summary: The comment and the substring index for the grant shortcut disagree with the encoding format.
suggestions.content: The comment says the grant shortcut "starts at character 4th char" and the code takes substring(3,5). The encoder lays out the prefix as sessionType (0-2), tokenType (2-4), grantType (4-6), so the grant shortcut starts at the 5th char, index 4. The comment, the code and the format all disagree. The equals branch also returns false on a match, which is the reverse of what describeTo() says. Use substring(4, 6), return false when the shortcut does not match, and fix the comment.
suggestions.summaryPt: O comentário e o índice da substring para o shortcut do grant discordam do formato de codificação.
suggestions.contentPt: O comentário diz que o shortcut do grant "starts at character 4th char" e o código usa substring(3,5). O encoder organiza o prefixo como sessionType (0-2), tokenType (2-4), grantType (4-6), então o shortcut do grant começa no 5º caractere, índice 4. O comentário, o código e o formato discordam entre si. O branch de equals também retorna false quando há correspondência, o que é o inverso do que describeTo() diz. Use substring(4, 6), retorne false quando o shortcut não corresponder e corrija o comentário.

suggestions.summary: isAccessTokenId reads the grant shortcut at the wrong offset and inverts the check, so it effectively accepts any grant type.
suggestions.content: The encoder writes the token id as sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2) + ':' + uuid, so the grant shortcut is at characters 4-6 (`substring(4, 6)`). The matcher instead takes `substring(3, 5)`, which spans the last character of the token type and the first character of the grant. It also returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut. In practice the substring almost never matches, so the matcher accepts any UUID-suffixed id and never checks the grant type. In the rare case where characters 3-5 do equal the shortcut, a correct id is rejected. Fix: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.
suggestions.summaryPt: isAccessTokenId lê o shortcut do grant no offset errado e inverte a verificação, então na prática aceita qualquer grant type.
suggestions.contentPt: O encoder escreve o token id como sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2) + ':' + uuid, então o shortcut do grant fica nos caracteres 4-6 (`substring(4, 6)`). Na prática, a substring quase nunca coincide, então o matcher aceita qualquer id com sufixo UUID e nunca verifica o grant type. No caso raro em que os caracteres 3-5 são iguais ao shortcut, um id correto é rejeitado. Correção: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

suggestions.content: WHAT: `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` compares an org-aware wrapped `original` (from `getById`) with the raw `updated` model. The wrapper's isEnabled() returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled, but the cached login ID lists come from `idpDelegate.getForLogin` and ignore org state. WHY: while an org is disabled, its public IDPs stay in the cached ORG_ONLY/ALL lists. If an admin then updates one of them to hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true or BROKER_PUBLIC=false, both sides fail the predicate and the first early return skips invalidation. After the org is re-enabled, the stale ID passes the bean's isEnabled() re-check and the hidden/private IDP appears on the login page. HOW: evaluate the original with the stored, unwrapped state, e.g. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId()), model)`. Alternatively, always invalidate when the original is org-linked.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` compara um `original` encapsulado e ciente de organização (vindo de `getById`) com o modelo `updated` bruto. O isEnabled() do wrapper retorna false sempre que a organização vinculada está desabilitada, mas as listas de IDs de login em cache vêm de `idpDelegate.getForLogin` e ignoram o estado da organização. POR QUÊ: enquanto uma organização está desabilitada, seus IDPs públicos permanecem nas listas em cache ORG_ONLY/ALL. Se um admin então atualizar um deles para hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true ou BROKER_PUBLIC=false, ambos os lados falham no predicado e o primeiro early return pula a invalidação. Depois que a organização é reabilitada, o ID obsoleto passa pela nova verificação de isEnabled() do bean e o IDP oculto/privado aparece na página de login. CORREÇÃO: avalie o original com o estado armazenado, sem o wrapper, por exemplo `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId()), model)`. Alternativamente, sempre invalide quando o original estiver vinculado a uma organização.

suggestions.content: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was moved from DetectorHandler, where it implemented evaluate as a stub, to StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler has abstract methods get_dedupe_value and get_group_key_values, and this PR adds a third, build_occurrence_and_event_data. suggestions.content: WHAT: tagDeviceUI writes the device to localCache (line 87) before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs, and it does not remove the entry when that call returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. suggestions.content: The device limit is enforced with a check-then-act sequence. CountDevices runs, then the insert runs in a separate statement with no transaction, lock or constraint. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. The PR also removed the async goroutine, so requests now tag in parallel. Fix: do the count and insert atomically, for example in one transaction with a lock, or with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit, or serialize through a server lock.
suggestions.contentPt: O limite de dispositivos é aplicado com uma sequência check-then-act. CountDevices é executado, depois o insert roda em uma instrução separada, sem transação, lock ou constraint. Requisições concorrentes de novos dispositivos podem todas ver count < limit e todas inserir, de modo que o limite é excedido. O PR também removeu a goroutine assíncrona, então as requisições agora fazem o tagging em paralelo. Correção: faça a contagem e o insert de forma atômica, por exemplo em uma única transação com lock, ou com um INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit condicional, ou serialize por meio de um lock no servidor.

suggestions.content: The local cache key is set (impl.go:87) before the store write. If tagDeviceUI fails, including with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key stays cached, so the device is probably treated as already tagged for the cache TTL (29 minutes) and later requests are not re-evaluated. The cache entry should be removed, or only set after a successful write.

A entrada do cache deve ser removida, ou definida somente após uma escrita bem-sucedida.

A rejected device then hits the cache for 29 minutes, tagDeviceUI returns nil, and the device limit is bypassed. Fix: set the cache entry only after a successful write, or delete the key on error.

All three suggestions describe the same defect, and the diff confirms it. The cache key is set at impl.go:87 before the database write and is not removed when the write fails. Because of that, a device rejected for ErrDeviceLimitReached gets past the limit for the 29-minute cache lifetime. All three also propose the same fix: write the cache entry only after the write succeeds, or delete it on error.

The line ranges differ (144-148 is where TagDevice now passes the error up; 87-95 is the cache write), but both are in the same file and both refer to the same cache line. One edit in tagDeviceUI fixes the whole thing, so the kind is same_location rather than cross_location.

suggestions.content: WHAT: No double-checked cache test is done after taking the write lock, and the cache is overwritten even when the read fails. WHY: Concurrent first requests all redo the manifest read serially, and a transient error stores nil in the cache, replacing a previously valid value. HOW: After Lock(), re-check `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`. Only assign the cache when err == nil.
suggestions.contentPt: O QUÊ: Não é feito nenhum teste de double-checked cache após adquirir o write lock, e o cache é sobrescrito mesmo quando a leitura falha. POR QUÊ: Primeiras requisições concorrentes refazem a leitura do manifest em série, e um erro transitório armazena nil no cache, substituindo um valor válido anterior. CORREÇÃO: Após o Lock(), verifique novamente `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`. Atribua o cache apenas quando err == nil.

Also, the assignment `entryPointAssetsCache = result` (line ~69) must only happen when err == nil. If `result` can be nil or partial on error, a failed load is stored in the cache and served to every later reader in non-dev mode. I did not read the function body between the lock and that assignment, so I could not confirm this path is reachable.

The judges disagreed only on needsUnifiedComment. Each member already covers both defects at the same place, so either one alone can replace the group without losing anything. The rule's wording about overlapping groups that report more than one defect could be read the other way, so this flag is a judgment call. That is why decisive is false.

suggestions.summary: isAccessTokenId matcher has an inverted comparison and the wrong substring offset.
suggestions.content: WHAT: The isAccessTokenId matcher has an inverted comparison and the wrong substring offset. It returns false when the shortcut equals the expected one, and it reads substring(3, 5) instead of the grant shortcut at substring(4, 6). WHY: Correct token IDs fail the match, and the check does not validate the grant shortcut as intended. The tests that use expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh and similar will fail. FIX: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`

POR QUÊ: IDs de token corretos falham na verificação, e a checagem não valida o grant shortcut como pretendido. Os testes que usam expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh e similares vão falhar. CORREÇÃO: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`

suggestions.content: WHAT: join() does `break` once the deadline has passed, so the remaining processes are never terminated. The `process.terminate()` call sits inside the loop after that `break`. WHY: with several processes and a timeout, a slow first process leaves later flusher processes running without terminate(). HOW: do not break; instead skip the wait loop when time is up and always call terminate() for each multiprocessing.Process (or run the terminate step in a separate pass after the wait loop).

WHAT: on restart, the old worker is only killed if it is a multiprocessing.Process. A hung threading.Thread (the produce_to_pipe case) cannot be stopped and keeps running while a replacement is started. WHY: two workers then flush the same shards and share the `stopped` and `current_drift` values. Also, `_create_process_for_shards` overwrites `self.buffers[process_index]` with a new SpansBuffer without closing the old one. HOW: signal the old worker to stop through a per-process flag, or only restart workers that are actually dead.

The `time.sleep(0.1)` added here is a no-op because `time.sleep` is monkeypatched to `lambda _: None` at the start of the test. It does not wait for the flusher thread, so the later `(msg,) = messages` assertion can run before the flusher has produced anything. Replace it with a condition-based wait: poll `messages` until it is non-empty with a deadline, using the real sleep captured before patching.

`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` uses a truthiness test, so an explicit 0 (valid for the int CLI option) is treated as unset and spawns one process per shard. Use an explicit None check, and validate values below 1: `self.max_processes = len(buffer.assigned_shards) if max_processes is None else max_processes`.

The docstring says 'Creates one process per shard', but the constructor now caps processes at min(max_processes, number of shards) and assigns shards round-robin. Several shards can share one process, and the CLI defaults to a single flusher process. Reword it, e.g. 'Creates up to max_processes processes; shards are distributed across them.'

The wait_produce timer is tagged with the key "shards". The other new metrics (flusher.produce, segment_size_bytes, flusher_unhealthy) use the key "shard". The tag key is inconsistent, so dashboards that group by "shard" will miss this metric. Use "shard" for all of them.

The restart path now kills the old process only if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes are created from `mp_context.Process`, where `mp_context` is the spawn context, so they are `SpawnProcess` objects. `SpawnProcess` is a `BaseProcess` subclass, not a subclass of `multiprocessing.context.Process`, so this check is likely always False. The old code called `kill()` unconditionally. A hung process is therefore never killed before a replacement is spawned, which leaks processes that keep flushing the same shards. Use `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` in the check, or call `kill()` for anything that is not a `threading.Thread`. The same check in `join()` means `terminate()` is also skipped.

The tag key is inconsistent across metrics. `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": ...}`. `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": ...}`. Metrics that should be sliced together will not line up. Use one key name, and note the value is a comma-joined list of shards.

The hung-process kill is guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process). The flusher processes are SpawnProcess objects, which are not instances of multiprocessing.Process, so the guard is False and kill() is never called. A hung flusher keeps running while _create_process_for_shards starts a second one on the same shards. Both read and flush the same Redis segments, which can cause duplicate production and leaked processes. Check for threading.Thread instead (for example `if not isinstance(process, threading.Thread): process.kill()`), or use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess. The same isinstance check in join() (the terminate call) has the same problem.

suggestions.content: `queued` defaults to `timezone.now()`, which is evaluated once when the module is imported. Every AssignmentSource instance therefore gets the same stale timestamp, not the time it was queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` (import `field` from dataclasses).

suggestions.content: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import, so every AssignmentSource shares the same stale timestamp (the process start time). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead. A datetime in to_dict() would also break if the Celery serializer were ever switched from pickle to JSON.
